Query_Text_cn: 医药：虚拟现实使科学家们能够在充满分子和其它物体图像的环境中工作，而以前要做到这一点则必需进行电子显微镜的观测。
Translation: Pharmaceuticals: Virtual reality enables scientists to work in environments filled with images of molecules and other objects, which previously required observation through electron microscopy.

Query_Text_cn: 研究人员们预示，受训的外科医生将能够在电子尸体上进行实习，而经验丰富的外科医生也可以从应用虚拟现实所发展的新技术中获益匪浅。
Translation: Researchers predict that trained surgeons will be able to practice on electronic cadavers, and experienced surgeons can also greatly benefit from new technologies developed through the application of virtual reality.

Query_Text_cn: “它对医学的影响是无限的，”戈德费瑟教授说。
Translation: "It has an unlimited impact on medicine," said Professor Goldfeather.

Query_Text_cn: 这些器官虽然只是计算机里的模型，但你会觉得你真的置身于人体的内部。
Translation: Although these organs are merely models within a computer, you will feel as if you are truly inside the human body.

Query_Text_cn: 当前这项技术的最大障碍来自如下事实：今天的计算机速度仍然不够快。一个十分值得注意的新发现给出计算机速度每十八个月到两年翻一番。
Translation: The biggest obstacle to this technology at present stems from the fact that today's computers are still not fast enough. A remarkable new discovery indicates that computer speed doubles every eighteen months to two years.

Query_Text_cn: 计算机科学家说，创造一个图像的各个部分需要进行巨大数量的运算。
Translation: Computer scientists say that creating each part of an image requires a tremendous amount of computation.

Query_Text_cn: 研究人员期望在今后五到十年里有大的突破。
Translation: Researchers expect major breakthroughs in the next five to ten years.

Query_Text_cn: “计算速度将提高到这样的水平，以致我们能创造更加精密复杂的图像，”菲什曼教授预测说。
Translation: Professor Fishman predicts, "The speed of computation will increase to such a level that we will be able to create more sophisticated and complex images."

Query_Text_cn: 而随着计算机机率的提高，人们期望虚拟现实系统难以接受的价格将会下降。
Translation: As computer capabilities improve, it is expected that the prohibitively high prices of virtual reality systems will decrease.

Query_Text_cn: 本文简介：一艘沿火星轨道运行，执行火星全球勘测者部分任务的宇宙飞船，将连续两年把勘测数据发送回地面。
Translation: Summary: A spacecraft operating along Mars' orbit and carrying out part of the Mars Global Surveyor mission will transmit survey data back to Earth continuously for two years.

Query_Text_cn: 来自这次勘测送回的有关被称为“红色星球”的火星的信息资料，将有助于科学家更多地了解我们的行星地球，以及揭示有关火星的新情况。
Translation: The information and data about Mars, known as the "Red Planet," sent back from this exploration will help scientists gain a deeper understanding of our own planet Earth and reveal new findings about Mars.

Query_Text_cn: 1996年11月，美国国家航空和航天局与美国喷气推进实验室发射了火星全球勘测者宇宙飞船，这是在中断了20年之后，美国又着手重新开始对火星的勘测。
Translation: In November 1996, NASA and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory launched the Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft, marking the United States' renewed efforts to explore Mars after a 20-year hiatus.

Query_Text_cn: 这一耗资1.54亿美元的勘测任务将为研究火星的科学工作开创一个新的令人振奋的时代。
Translation: This $154 million survey mission will usher in an exciting new era for scientific research on Mars.

Query_Text_cn: 在整个火星年期间，勘测者号将发回前所未有的大量有关火星地貌、大气环境以及磁场特性的数据。
Translation: Throughout the entire Martian year, the Surveyor will transmit an unprecedented amount of data on Mars' topography, atmospheric conditions, and magnetic field characteristics.

Query_Text_cn: 科学家将利用这次勘测所收集的数据，通过地球与火星的比较，既可了解地球，又可以建立一种综合数据集来帮助制定未来的勘测计划。
Translation: Scientists will use the data collected from this survey to gain insights into Earth through comparisons with Mars, while also establishing a comprehensive dataset to assist in formulating future exploration plans.

Query_Text_cn: 勘测者号宇宙飞船于1996年11月7日在佛罗里达州卡纳维拉尔角空军基地由“德尔它一7925”火箭发射升空。
Translation: The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was launched on November 7, 1996, from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida aboard a Delta II 7925 rocket.

Query_Text_cn: 该飞船由洛克希德马丁航空公司制造，重量为1062公斤，经300多天航行，近7.5亿公里(约__UNDEF__4.66亿英里)航程，飞船于__UNDEF__1997年9月12日到达火星。
Translation: The spacecraft, manufactured by Lockheed Martin Aeronautics, weighed 1,062 kilograms. After traveling for more than 300 days and covering a distance of nearly 750 million kilometers (about 466 million miles), the spacecraft arrived at Mars on September 12, 1997.

Query_Text_cn: 抵达火星的瞬时，勘测者号即点燃主火箭发动机，开始25分钟的进入火星轨道的运行，这种机动动作放慢了飞船的速度以便火星的引力使飞船进入轨道。勘测者号开始在一个__UNDEF__48小时运行一周的精确椭圆轨道上，绕着别名为“红色星球”的火星运行。进入轨道之后，勘测者号开始进行一系列的轨道变化，以便把轨道近地点降到高度约110公里的火星大气层的上边缘位置。在每一次通过大气层期间，由于空气的阻力，飞船的速度开始略有放慢。这种减速使飞船在下一次通过轨道远地点时降低原有的高度。
Translation: At the moment of arrival at Mars, the Surveyor ignited its main rocket engine and began a 25-minute maneuver to enter Martian orbit. This maneuver slowed the spacecraft so that Mars' gravity could capture it into orbit. The Surveyor initially entered a precise elliptical orbit around the "Red Planet," completing one revolution every 48 hours. After entering orbit, the Surveyor began a series of orbital adjustments to lower its periapsis to about 110 kilometers, just above the upper edge of the Martian atmosphere. During each pass through the atmosphere, the spacecraft's speed was slightly reduced due to air resistance. This deceleration caused the spacecraft to lower its original altitude at the next apoapsis passage.

Query_Text_cn: 勘测者号使用这种创新的“空气制动”技术，经过四个月时间使轨道远地点高度从56000公里下降到约400公里的高度。
Translation: Using this innovative "aerobraking" technology, Mars Global Surveyor reduced its orbital apoapsis from 56,000 kilometers to approximately 400 kilometers over a period of four months.

Query_Text_cn: 这次任务的测绘阶段计划于1998年3月中旬开始。
Translation: The surveying phase of this project is scheduled to begin in mid-March 1998.

Query_Text_cn: 测绘期间，飞船每118分钟绕火星运行一周，平均高度为378公里。
Translation: During the survey period, the spacecraft orbited Mars once every 118 minutes at an average altitude of 378 kilometers.

Query_Text_cn: 在687个地球日里，勘测者号将利用这种轨道的有利位置连续不断地收集科学数据。
Translation: Over the course of 687 Earth days, Surveyor will take advantage of this favorable orbital position to continuously collect scientific data.

Query_Text_cn: 勘测工作中将使用许多科学仪器。
Translation: Many scientific instruments will be used in the survey work.

Query_Text_cn: 摄像机将每天拍摄与每晚电视新闻中播放的地球气象图相似的火星广角图像。
Translation: The camera will capture wide-angle images of Mars every day, similar to the Earth weather maps shown in nightly television news broadcasts.

Query_Text_cn: 此外，摄像机的窄角镜头还会拍摄小至1.5米宽的物体图像。
Translation: In addition, the camera's narrow-angle lens can capture images of objects as small as 1.5 meters wide.

Query_Text_cn: 激光测高仪通过物体表面反射的光束测量山脉的高度和峡谷的深度。
Translation: A laser altimeter measures the height of mountains and the depth of valleys by detecting light beams reflected from the surface of objects.

Query_Text_cn: 热辐射光谱仪将扫描记录火星释放出的热量以便研究大气层，测绘火星表面的矿物成分。
Translation: The thermal emission spectrometer will scan and record the heat emitted by Mars to study its atmosphere and map the mineral composition of its surface.

Query_Text_cn: 地磁仪研究火星的磁场特性，以了解该星体的内部结构。
Translation: Magnetometers are used to study the magnetic properties of Mars in order to understand its internal structure.

Query_Text_cn: 2000年1月下旬完成测绘工作之后，飞船将作为一颗通信卫星使用。在火星着陆的地面运行装置承担部分未来火星研究任务，它所收集的数据将经过这颗通信卫星中继发回地球。
Translation: After completing the mapping work in late January 2000, the spacecraft will be used as a communications satellite. The surface rover that lands on Mars will undertake part of the future Mars research tasks, and the data it collects will be relayed back to Earth via this communications satellite.

Query_Text_cn: 火星全球勘测者任务将取得的最重要的成果之一就是通过火星和地球的比较，可以使科学家子解地球的历史和它未来可能发展的趋势。
Translation: One of the most important achievements of the Mars Global Surveyor mission is that, by comparing Mars and Earth, scientists can better understand the history of our own planet and the possible trends in its future development.

Query_Text_cn: 在它们几十亿年前形成的时候，火星和地球上的环境相似。
Translation: When they formed billions of years ago, the environments on Mars and Earth were similar.

Query_Text_cn: 两个星体都蕴藏着大量的表层水，厚厚的大气层，而且气候比现在温和。
Translation: Both celestial bodies contain abundant surface water, thick atmospheres, and a milder climate than they have today.

Query_Text_cn: 如今地球是一个繁荣昌盛的世界，它拥有数不清的动植物物种。
Translation: Today, Earth is a thriving and prosperous world, home to countless species of plants and animals.

Query_Text_cn: 相反，过去30多年从火星上收集的数据资料表明，该星体陷入的困境使人联想到地球冰河时代。
Translation: In contrast, data collected from Mars over the past 30 years suggest that the planet's predicament is reminiscent of Earth's Ice Age.

Query_Text_cn: 把干燥得似乎没有生命的火星表面和看上去像是一片汪洋大海的撒哈拉沙漠加以比较，把火星日平均气温和南极洲曾有过的温和气候相对比，通过两个星球之间的历史和演化过程的比较，可以找出地球的历史线索和它未来可能发展的趋势。
Translation: By comparing the seemingly lifeless, arid surface of Mars with the Sahara Desert, which appears like a vast ocean, and contrasting the average daily temperature on Mars with the mild climate that once existed in Antarctica, we can, through the comparative study of the histories and evolutionary processes of the two planets, uncover clues about Earth's own history and the possible trends of its future development.

Query_Text_cn: 尽管火星上的气候恶劣，但火星和任何其它行星相比，它的表面温度与地球的表面温度更加相似。
Translation: Despite the harsh climate on Mars, its surface temperature is more similar to that of Earth than any other planet.

Query_Text_cn: 气温上的这些相似之处部分是由于存在这样的事实：与其它星球相比，火星的轨道与太阳的距离只比地球与太阳的距离稍远一点。
Translation: These similarities in temperature are partly due to the fact that, compared to other planets, Mars's orbit is only slightly farther from the Sun than Earth's orbit.

Query_Text_cn: 例如，火星赤道附近一些地点的地面温度中午时分可高达摄氏25度。
Translation: For example, at certain locations near the Martian equator, ground temperatures can reach as high as 25 degrees Celsius at noon.

Query_Text_cn: 然而，白天的平均温度仍然在冰点以下，晚上的温度则更低些。
Translation: However, the average daytime temperature remains below freezing, and it drops even lower at night.

Query_Text_cn: 火星上的温度看起来可能对训练有素的户外勘探者有相当大的诱惑力，但从人类的观点看，大气成分还有许多欠缺。
Translation: The temperatures on Mars may seem quite appealing to well-trained outdoor explorers, but from a human perspective, the atmospheric composition still leaves much to be desired.

Query_Text_cn: 火星上的空气大部分是由二氧化碳组成的，与金星的情况相似。
Translation: The atmosphere on Mars is mostly composed of carbon dioxide, similar to the situation on Venus.

Query_Text_cn: 如果说呼吸二氧化碳令人生厌的话，那么空气的密度就显得更为糟糕。
Translation: If breathing carbon dioxide is unpleasant, then the density of air is even worse.

Query_Text_cn: 据检测，火星上的平均大气压低至地球海平面的平均大气压的l／125。
Translation: According to measurements, the average atmospheric pressure on Mars is as low as 1/125 of the average atmospheric pressure at sea level on Earth.

Query_Text_cn: 换句话说，火星表面的空气比科罗拉多州丹佛市的高度再高19倍的地方的空气更稀薄。
Translation: In other words, the air on the surface of Mars is even thinner than the air at an altitude 19 times higher than that of Denver, Colorado.

Query_Text_cn: 火星上极度稀薄的空气使火星上无论是过去还是现在是否有生命这一问题更加神秘化了。
Translation: The extremely thin atmosphere on Mars adds further mystery to the question of whether life has ever existed or currently exists on the planet.

Query_Text_cn: 其原因是几乎所有的水都蕴藏在火星南北两极的冰盖下或冻结在表层下面。
Translation: The reason is that almost all the water is stored beneath the polar ice caps at the north and south poles of Mars or is frozen beneath the surface layer.

Query_Text_cn: 液体的水不可能存在于表面上，因为稀薄的空气将融化着的冰直接蒸发成为水蒸气。
Translation: Liquid water cannot exist on the surface because the thin atmosphere causes melting ice to evaporate directly into water vapor.

Query_Text_cn: 科学家把这一过程称之为“升华作用”。
Translation: Scientists refer to this process as "sublimation."

Query_Text_cn: 虽然火星上的液体水会很快蒸发，但国家航空和航天局以前勘测火星时发回到地面上的照片显示，火星表面上有一些洪水流过的巨大沟渠，干枯的河床及漫滩地带。
Translation: Although liquid water on Mars would evaporate quickly, photos sent back to Earth during previous Mars explorations by NASA have shown that there are massive channels carved by floods, dried-up riverbeds, and alluvial plains on the surface of Mars.

Query_Text_cn: 火星上过去曾经有过水这一迹象，使得某些科学家认为寻找外星生命，火星是太阳系内一个主要地点。
Translation: The evidence that water once existed on Mars has led some scientists to believe that Mars is a primary location within the solar system for searching for extraterrestrial life.

Query_Text_cn: 因为数十亿年前火星曾一度有过较稠密的大气层和大量的表面水，人们推测尽管火星现在的气候恶劣，但可能蕴藏着有利于生命形成的环境。
Translation: Because Mars had a relatively dense atmosphere and abundant surface water billions of years ago, it is speculated that, despite its harsh current climate, the planet may still harbor environments conducive to the emergence of life.

Query_Text_cn: 在过去的30多年里，国家航空和航天局向火星发射了不同的宇宙飞船，它们携带的一些传感器业已表明，目前该星体上几乎肯定不存在高级形式的生命。
Translation: Over the past 30 years, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration has launched various spacecraft to Mars, and some of the sensors they carried have already indicated that there is almost certainly no advanced form of life currently on the planet.

Query_Text_cn: 然而，人们仍然认为火星上可能隐藏着细菌形式的生命或它们的残遗化石。
Translation: However, it is still believed that Mars may harbor bacterial forms of life or their fossilized remnants.

Query_Text_cn: 虽然火星全球勘测者将不用于寻找火星上的生命，但它会收集详尽的数据资料以帮助了解火星水消失之谜。
Translation: Although the Mars Global Surveyor will not be used to search for life on Mars, it will collect detailed data to help unravel the mystery of the disappearance of water on the planet.

Query_Text_cn: 这种研究将提供重要的背景材料，它们会有助于科学家们在未来的勘测工作中寻找火星上的生命。
Translation: This research will provide important background materials that will help scientists in their future exploration efforts to search for life on Mars.

Query_Text_cn: 从地质上来讲，火星也是太阳系中最能引起人们兴趣的星体之一。
Translation: Geologically speaking, Mars is also one of the most intriguing celestial bodies in the solar system.

Query_Text_cn: 这一小小的呈红色的多岩石星体，大小是月球的两倍，但只是地球的一半。
Translation: This small, reddish, rocky celestial body is twice the size of the Moon but only half the size of the Earth.

Query_Text_cn: 尽管其体积很小，但它的南北两极有大量的水和二氧化碳冰盖；它有一条比美国科罗拉多大峡谷还要深，比美国国土还要长的峡谷；它的一些火山形成的凹谷，面积与美国整个西部地区相当；少数巨大奇异的火山即便是珠穆朗玛峰与之相比，也显得相形见绌。
Translation: Despite its small size, it has massive water and carbon dioxide ice caps at its north and south poles; it boasts a canyon deeper than the Grand Canyon in Colorado and longer than the entire United States; some of its volcanic calderas cover an area comparable to the entire western United States; and a few of its enormous and unusual volcanoes make even Mount Everest pale in comparison.

Query_Text_cn: 研究火星地质对于揭示地球历史演变的蛛丝马迹是十分重要的。
Translation: Studying Martian geology is crucial for uncovering clues about the historical evolution of Earth.

Query_Text_cn: 其原因是火星在太阳系中是唯一具备以下特征的星体，它既有大气层，又有几乎覆盖整个历史演变的地貌。
Translation: The reason is that Mars is the only celestial body in the solar system that possesses the following characteristics: it has an atmosphere and landforms that almost cover its entire evolutionary history.

Query_Text_cn: 就地球来说，因为地质变迁，气候及生命引起的巨大变化，我们这个星球实体在最初十亿年所形成的原始岩石和其它地貌现已不复存在了。
Translation: As far as the Earth is concerned, due to geological changes, as well as significant transformations caused by climate and life, the original rocks and other landforms formed during the first billion years of our planet's existence have now disappeared.

Query_Text_cn: 因为地球和火星在接近形成时的境况相同，所以勘测火星将会使我们得以窥视地球的过去，这是通过地球本身来研究地球所不可能做到的。
Translation: Because Earth and Mars had similar conditions during their formation, exploring Mars will allow us to glimpse Earth's past—something that cannot be achieved by studying Earth itself.

Query_Text_cn: 要谈论宇宙的本质和讨论它是否有开端或终结这样的问题，人们必须弄清什么是科学理论。
Translation: To discuss the nature of the universe and questions such as whether it has a beginning or an end, one must first understand what a scientific theory is.

Query_Text_cn: 用简单的思维方式，可以说理论不过是关于宇宙的模式或关于它的某一有限部分的模式，以及一整套把这个模式中的量与我们观测的结果联系起来的规则。
Translation: In simple terms, a theory can be described as a model of the universe, or of a limited part of it, together with a set of rules that relate quantities in the model to the results of our observations.

Query_Text_cn: 它仅存于我们的思维之中，没有任何实体(无论何种意义的)。
Translation: It exists only in our minds and has no physical entity whatsoever (in any sense).

Query_Text_cn: 一个理论若能满足以下两个条件，就是有意义的：首先它必须在只含有几个任意元素的基础上能对大部分观测现象进行精确的描述，其次它必须对未来的观测结果作出明确的预言。
Translation: A theory is meaningful if it meets the following two criteria: first, it must be able to provide an accurate description of most observed phenomena based on only a few arbitrary elements; second, it must make clear predictions about future observations.

Query_Text_cn: 例如，亚里士多德的关于一切物质都是由土、气、火和水这四元素组成的理论是再简单不过的了，但它没有任何明确的预言。
Translation: For example, Aristotle's theory that all matter is composed of the four elements—earth, air, fire, and water—is extremely simple, but it contains no explicit predictions.

Query_Text_cn: 另一方面，牛顿的引力理论是基于更为简单的模式，即物体之间的吸引力与质量成正比，与它们之间距离的平方成反比，但它却以很高的精确度预示了太阳、月亮和行星的运动。
Translation: On the other hand, Newton's theory of gravitation is based on a much simpler model: the attractive force between objects is directly proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. Nevertheless, it predicts the motions of the sun, moon, and planets with remarkable accuracy.

Query_Text_cn: 任何物理理论都是暂时的，因为它只是一种假设：人们永远不可能也证明它。
Translation: Any physical theory is provisional, as it is merely a hypothesis: it can never be proven.

Query_Text_cn: 不管某一理论如何与多少回的实验结果相一致，你决不能断定这一理论将与下一次实验结果不会有矛盾。
Translation: No matter how well a theory aligns with numerous experimental results, you can never conclude that it will not contradict the outcome of the next experiment.

Query_Text_cn: 另一方面，人们只要发现一个观测结果与理论预言不一致，就可以否定那种理论。
Translation: On the other hand, as long as an observation is found to be inconsistent with a theoretical prediction, that theory can be refuted.

Query_Text_cn: 正如科学哲学家卡尔·波普强调的那样，一个好的理论，其特征是能作出许多原则上可以被观测结果所否定或证伪的预言。
Translation: As the philosopher of science Karl Popper emphasized, a good theory is characterized by its ability to make numerous predictions that can, in principle, be refuted or falsified by observational results.

Query_Text_cn: 然而，一旦某一次新的观测与之不符，我们就得放弃或修改这一理论。
Translation: However, if a new observation contradicts it, we must abandon or modify the theory.

Query_Text_cn: 至少这是人们所认为的发展模式会发生，但你总是可以怀疑做出这种观测的人的能力。
Translation: At least this is how people believe the development model will unfold, but one can always question the competence of those making such observations.

Query_Text_cn: 实际上，通常发生的情况是，一种新的理论的诞生的确是对原先理论的拓展。
Translation: In fact, what usually happens is that the emergence of a new theory does indeed serve as an extension of the original theory.

Query_Text_cn: 例如，对水星非常精确的观测揭示了它的运动与牛顿引力理论的预言略有不同。
Translation: For example, highly precise observations of Mercury have revealed that its motion differs slightly from the predictions of Newton's theory of gravity.

Query_Text_cn: 爱因斯坦的广义相对论所预言的运动与牛顿理论稍有差异。
Translation: The motion predicted by Einstein's general theory of relativity differs slightly from that predicted by Newton's theory.

Query_Text_cn: 爱因斯坦的预言与观测相符，而牛顿的与观测不相符，这一事实是新理论成立的一个关键证据。
Translation: The fact that Einstein's predictions matched observations while Newton's did not is a key piece of evidence supporting the validity of the new theory.

Query_Text_cn: 然而，在所有实用场合我们仍然使用牛顿的理论，因为在我们正常遇见的情况中，牛顿的预言与广义相对论的差异非常小。
Translation: However, in all practical situations, we still use Newton's theory because, under normal circumstances, the differences between Newton's predictions and those of general relativity are extremely small.

Query_Text_cn: (牛顿理论还有一个巨大的优点，即应用起来比爱因斯坦的理论要简单得多。
Translation: Newton's theory has another significant advantage: it is much simpler to apply than Einstein's theory.

Query_Text_cn: 科学的最终目标是发现描述整个宇宙的单一理论。
Translation: The ultimate goal of science is to discover a single theory that describes the entire universe.

Query_Text_cn: 然而，大部分科学家实际遵循的方法是将这个问题分成两部分。
Translation: However, most scientists actually approach this issue by dividing it into two parts.

Query_Text_cn: 第一部分是那些告诉我们宇宙如何随时间而演变的定律。
Translation: The first part consists of the laws that tell us how the universe evolves over time.

Query_Text_cn: （如果我们已知在任一时刻宇宙是什么样子，那么这些定律就能告诉我们它在未来的任一时刻将是什么样子。）第二部分是关于宇宙初始状态的问题。
Translation: (If we know what the universe is like at any given moment, these laws can tell us what it will be like at any future moment.) The second part concerns the question of the initial state of the universe.

Query_Text_cn: 他们认为初始状态的问题是玄学或宗教的范畴。
Translation: They believe that the question of the initial state falls within the realm of metaphysics or religion.

Query_Text_cn: 他们会说，万能的上帝完全可以随心所欲地启动宇宙。
Translation: They would say that an omnipotent God could set the universe in motion entirely at His will.

Query_Text_cn: 但上帝好像选择了让宇宙以一种非常规则的、按照一定规律运动的方式在演化。
Translation: But it seems that God has chosen to let the universe evolve in a very orderly manner, following certain laws and patterns.

Query_Text_cn: 因此，假定在宇宙初始状态也有制约它的法则，看起来同样是合理的。
Translation: Therefore, it also seems reasonable to assume that there were laws governing the initial state of the universe.

Query_Text_cn: 要想一步登天地提出一种能描述整个宇宙的理论看起来是非常困难的。
Translation: It seems extremely difficult to propose a theory that can describe the entire universe in one leap.

Query_Text_cn: 相反我们将这个问题加以解剖并提出许多局部理论。
Translation: On the contrary, we dissect this issue and propose a number of partial theories.

Query_Text_cn: 每一个局部理论只描述和预言一定范围的有限的观测，而忽略其它量的效应或仅以简单的一组数来代指它们。
Translation: Each local theory only describes and predicts a limited range of observations, while ignoring the effects of other variables or representing them with a simple set of numbers.

Query_Text_cn: 或许这种方法是完全错误的。
Translation: Perhaps this approach is entirely wrong.

Query_Text_cn: 如果宇宙中的每一个物体从根本上就依赖于其它物体，那么孤立地研究问题的一部分也许不可能得到完备的答案。
Translation: If every object in the universe fundamentally depends on other objects, then studying only a part of a problem in isolation may not yield a complete answer.

Query_Text_cn: 尽管如此，这的确又是我们以往取得进展所用的方法。
Translation: Nevertheless, this is indeed the approach we have used to make progress in the past.

Query_Text_cn: 典型的例子还是牛顿的引力理论，它告诉我们两个物体之间的引力只取决于与每个物体相关的一个数——它的质量，而与物体由什么组成无关。
Translation: A typical example is Newton's theory of gravity, which tells us that the gravitational force between two objects depends only on a single number associated with each object—its mass—and is unrelated to what the objects are made of.

Query_Text_cn: 依此，人们要计算太阳和行星的轨迹，并不需要于其结构和成分的理论。
Translation: Accordingly, to calculate the trajectories of the sun and planets, one does not need a theory of their structure and composition.

Query_Text_cn: 今天科学家们按照两种基本的局部理论——广义相对论和量子力学来描述宇宙。
Translation: Today, scientists describe the universe based on two fundamental local theories: general relativity and quantum mechanics.

Query_Text_cn: 它们是本世纪上半叶的巨大智力成就。
Translation: They are remarkable intellectual achievements of the first half of this century.

Query_Text_cn: 广义相对论描述了引力和宇宙的大尺度结构，即这种结构尺度可以从只有几英里大到1亿亿亿(1后面有24个0)英里，即人类可观测的宇宙空间。
Translation: General relativity describes gravity and the large-scale structure of the universe, with this structure ranging in scale from just a few miles to 100,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000 (a 1 followed by 24 zeros) miles, which is the extent of the observable universe for humans.

Query_Text_cn: 另一方面，量子力学解决的问题是极小尺度里的现象，例如万亿亿分之一英寸。
Translation: On the other hand, quantum mechanics addresses phenomena at extremely small scales, such as one hundred quintillionth of an inch.

Query_Text_cn: 然而，遗憾的是人们已知这两种理论并不是一致的——它们不可能都正确：当代物理学的一个主攻方向，就是找一个新的能使两者合二为一的理论——量子引力论。
Translation: However, regrettably, it is known that these two theories are not consistent—they cannot both be correct. One of the main directions in contemporary physics is to seek a new theory that can unify them—quantum gravity.

Query_Text_cn: 我们还没有这样的理论，要获得这样的理论我们也许还有相当长的路要走，然而我们已经知道了这个理论应具备的许多特性。
Translation: We do not yet have such a theory, and it may still be a long way before we obtain one. However, we already know many of the characteristics that this theory should possess.

Query_Text_cn: 追溯物理学的起源就象寻找许多大江长河的发源地一样十分困难。
Translation: Tracing the origins of physics is as difficult as searching for the sources of many great rivers.

Query_Text_cn: 山坡上哗哗淌下的水流聚成小河,小河又汇成真正的“河流”。
Translation: The water flowing down the hillside gathers into a small stream, which then merges to form a real "river."

Query_Text_cn: 河床越变越宽，随着支流的不断加入最后变成了汹涌澎湃的巨流—变成密西西比河或伏尔加河，尼罗河或亚马逊河——最后注入大洋之中。
Translation: The riverbed grows wider and wider, and with the continuous addition of tributaries, it eventually becomes a surging torrent—a mighty river like the Mississippi or the Volga, the Nile or the Amazon—which ultimately flows into the ocean.

Query_Text_cn: 使物理学大河诞生的小溪遍布在人类居住的整个地面上但其中多数似乎是集中在巴尔干半岛岛南端,那里居住的人们我们今天称之为“古希腊人”，至少在我们这些继承了那些早期“知识分子”的文化的人看来是如此。
Translation: The streams that gave birth to the great river of physics are scattered across the lands inhabited by humans, but most of them seem to converge at the southern tip of the Balkan Peninsula, where the people we now refer to as "ancient Greeks" lived—at least, this is how it appears to those of us who have inherited the culture of those early "intellectuals."

Query_Text_cn: 值得注意的是，虽然其它的古代民族，例如巴比伦人和埃及人，对数学和天文学的早期发展做出了巨大贡献，但对物理学的发展却是毫无作为的。
Translation: It is worth noting that although other ancient civilizations, such as the Babylonians and Egyptians, made significant contributions to the early development of mathematics and astronomy, they made no contribution to the development of physics.

Query_Text_cn: 同希腊科学比较起来之所以有这种缺陷，一种可能的解释是:巴比伦人和埃及人的上帝都高居在九天之外，而古希腊的诸神却生活在海拔只有10,000英尺左右的奥林匹斯山之巅，这样，要了解地球上的问题就接近得多了。
Translation: Compared with Greek science, one possible explanation for this deficiency is that the gods of the Babylonians and Egyptians resided high above the nine heavens, whereas the gods of ancient Greece lived atop Mount Olympus, which is only about 10,000 feet above sea level. This made them much closer to understanding earthly matters.

Query_Text_cn: 传说“磁学”一词就是起一个牧羊人的名字，他惊奇地发现，他的包着铁皮的牧杖被路旁的一块石头吸过去了（磁铁石）。
Translation: It is said that the term "magnetism" originated from the name of a shepherd who was astonished to find his iron-tipped staff attracted by a stone (magnetite) by the roadside.

Query_Text_cn: 尽管这些传说很难找到什么确凿的证据，但公元前六世纪中叶的希腊哲学家毕达格拉斯的发现是有据可査的。
Translation: Although it is difficult to find any definitive evidence for these legends, the discoveries of the Greek philosopher Pythagoras in the mid-sixth century BC are well documented.

Query_Text_cn: 他确信世界是由数字主宰的，并研究了乐器上琴弦的长度之间的关系，这些琴弦能产生和谐的乐声。
Translation: He was convinced that the world is governed by numbers and studied the relationships between the lengths of strings on musical instruments, which could produce harmonious sounds.

Query_Text_cn: 为此，他使用的是所谓一弦琴，即一根长度可以变化的弦，并用悬挂重物的办法使它受到不同的张力。
Translation: To achieve this, he used what is known as a monochord—a single string whose length can be adjusted—and applied varying tension by suspending different weights.

Query_Text_cn: 他用同样的重物而改变弦长，发现当弦长之间有简单的数字关系时，就可得到一对对谐音。
Translation: He used the same weight but changed the length of the strings, and found that when the lengths of the strings had simple numerical relationships, pairs of harmonious tones could be produced.

Query_Text_cn: 2：1的弦长对应于大家都知道的八音度，3：2对应第五音，4：3对应笫四音。
Translation: A string length ratio of 2:1 corresponds to the well-known octave, 3:2 corresponds to the perfect fifth, and 4:3 corresponds to the perfect fourth.

Query_Text_cn: 这一发现大概是物理定律的第一次数学公式表示，完全可以认为是今天所谓理论物理学发展的第一步。
Translation: This discovery was probably the first mathematical formulation of a physical law and can be regarded as the first step in the development of what is now known as theoretical physics.

Query_Text_cn: 用现代的物理术语来说，我们可以这样表述毕达格拉斯的发现：在给定的张力作用下，一根给定弦的频率（即每秒内振动的次数）与其长度成反比。
Translation: In modern physical terms, we can express Pythagoras's discovery as follows: under a given tension, the frequency of a given string (that is, the number of vibrations per second) is inversely proportional to its length.

Query_Text_cn: 因此，如果第二根弦的长度是第一根弦的长度的一半，它的振动頻率就高一倍。
Translation: Therefore, if the length of the second string is half that of the first string, its vibration frequency will be twice as high.

Query_Text_cn: 如杲两根弦长成3:2或4:3的比例，它们的振动频率就成2：3或3：4之比。
Translation: If the lengths of two strings are in the ratio of 3:2 or 4:3, their vibration frequencies will be in the ratio of 2:3 or 3:4, respectively.

Query_Text_cn: 因为人脑中从耳朵接受神经信号的那一部分的构造使得只有简单的频率比——例如3：4——才是“悦耳的”，而复杂的比例一一例如137：171——则是“刺耳的”（这要等将来的大脑生理学家来解释这个事实了），所以要得到完美的和音，弦长必须成简革的数字比关系。
Translation: Because the structure of the part of the human brain that receives neural signals from the ears makes only simple frequency ratios—such as 3:4—"pleasant," while complex ratios—such as 137:171—are "harsh" (this fact awaits explanation from future neurophysiologists), perfect harmony requires that string lengths be in simple numerical ratios.

Query_Text_cn: 毕达格拉斯试图向前更进一步，他提出：因为行星的运动“必须是和谐的”它们到地球的距离也一定与希腊民族乐器七弦琴上产生七个基音的琴弦（在同样的张力下）的长度一样，有相同的比例关系。
Translation: Pythagoras sought to go further, proposing that since the motion of the planets "must be harmonious," their distances from the Earth must correspond to the lengths of the seven strings on the Greek seven-stringed lyre, which produce seven fundamental tones under the same tension, sharing the same proportional relationships.

Query_Text_cn: 另一个重要的理论是由大约公元前400年的另一位古希腊哲学家狄谟克瑞特提出的。用现代术语来说，这个理论可以称之为“没有任何实验基础的理论”，但事实是，“梦话道出了真情”。狄谟克瑞特所抱的观念是认为所有的物体都由数不清的、小得人眼无法看到的粒子集合而成的。
Translation: Another important theory was proposed by Democritus, another ancient Greek philosopher around 400 BC. In modern terms, this theory could be described as "a theory without any experimental basis," but in fact, "sleep talk revealed the truth." Democritus believed that all objects are composed of countless particles so small that they are invisible to the human eye.

Query_Text_cn: 他把这些粒子称为“原子”，在希腊语中就是“不可分的”意思，因为他相信这些粒子代表着把物体分为越来越小的部分的最后阶段。
Translation: He called these particles "atoms," which in Greek means "indivisible," because he believed they represented the final stage of dividing objects into increasingly smaller parts.

Query_Text_cn: 他认为有四种不同的原子，即石原子，干燥而重；水原子，重而潮湿;气原子，冷而轻；火原子，易变而热。
Translation: He believed there were four different types of atoms: earth atoms, which are dry and heavy; water atoms, which are heavy and moist; air atoms, which are cold and light; and fire atoms, which are mutable and hot.

Query_Text_cn: 他认为这四种不同的原子结合起来，就造成了所有已知的物质。
Translation: He believed that the combination of these four different types of atoms resulted in all known substances.

Query_Text_cn: 土壤是石原子与水原子的结合。
Translation: Soil is a combination of stone atoms and water atoms.

Query_Text_cn: 在阳光照耀下从土壤中生长出来的植物是土壤中的石原子和水原子与太阳中来的火原子结合而成的。
Translation: Plants that grow from the soil under sunlight are formed by the combination of stone atoms and water atoms from the soil with fire atoms from the sun.

Query_Text_cn: 这就是为什么干燥的枯木在失去其所有的水原子时会燃烧的原因，燃烧时放出火原子（火焰），而只剰下石原子（灰烬）。
Translation: This is why dry, dead wood burns when it loses all its water atoms, releasing fire atoms (flames) during combustion and leaving behind only stone atoms (ash).

Query_Text_cn: 当我们把某种石块（金属矿石）放入火焰时，石原子就与火原子结合在一起产生出称为金属的物质。
Translation: When we place a certain type of stone (metal ore) into a flame, the atoms of the stone combine with the atoms of the fire to produce a substance known as metal.

Query_Text_cn: 象铁那样廉价的金属，因为所含的火原子数量很少，所以显得有些笨重，金子含火原子最多，所以灿烂夺目而价值昂贵。
Translation: Metals as inexpensive as iron appear somewhat dull and heavy because they contain very few fire atoms, while gold, which contains the most fire atoms, is brilliant and valuable.

Query_Text_cn: 如果一个学生在他的初等化学考试中讲这些话，他肯定会得零分。
Translation: If a student said these things in his elementary chemistry exam, he would definitely get a zero.

Query_Text_cn: 然而，关于化学变化本性的这些特例虽然无疑是错误的，但只用少数基本的化学元素的组合来得到几乎无数种不同物质的基本思想，却是完全正确的，并且现已成为当代化学的基础。
Translation: However, although these specific cases concerning the nature of chemical changes are undoubtedly incorrect, the fundamental idea of obtaining an almost infinite variety of different substances through the combination of only a few basic chemical elements is entirely correct and has now become the foundation of modern chemistry.

Query_Text_cn: 但是，从狄谟克瑞特时代到道尔顿的时代，花了22个世纪的光阴才把事情弄清楚。
Translation: However, it took twenty-two centuries to clarify the matter, from the time of Democritus to the era of Dalton.

Query_Text_cn: 亚里斯多德是古代希腊世界的巨人之一。他的成名有两方面的原因:其一，因为他是一位真正的天才;第二，因为他曾任马其顿的亚历山大大帝的私人教师，后来又成了亚历山大大帝的门徒。
Translation: Aristotle was one of the giants of the ancient Greek world. His fame stemmed from two factors: first, he was a true genius; second, he served as the private tutor to Alexander the Great of Macedonia and later became a disciple of Alexander.

Query_Text_cn: 他在公元前384年生于爱琴海上一个希腊的殖民城市斯塔基拉，出身子一个原先是马其顿王室宫廷医师的家庭。
Translation: He was born in 384 BC in Stagira, a Greek colonial city on the Aegean Sea, into a family whose ancestors had served as court physicians to the Macedonian royal family.

Query_Text_cn: 十七岁的时候，他去雅典加入了柏拉图的哲学学派，并一直是柏拉图的热心追随者，直到柏拉图于公元前347年去世。
Translation: At the age of seventeen, he went to Athens to join Plato's school of philosophy and remained an enthusiastic follower of Plato until Plato's death in 347 BC.

Query_Text_cn: 此后，亚里斯多德进行了广泛的周游，最后又回到了雅典，在里西姆创立了当时称为“逍遥学派”的哲学学派。
Translation: Afterwards, Aristotle traveled extensively and eventually returned to Athens, where he founded the philosophical school known at the time as the "Peripatetic School" at the Lyceum.

Query_Text_cn: 流传至今的大多数亚里斯多德的著作,差不多都是他在里西姆传授各门科学时的讲稿。
Translation: Most of Aristotle's works that have been passed down to this day are almost all lecture notes from his teachings on various sciences at the Lyceum.

Query_Text_cn: 其中有关于他所创建的逻辑学和心理学的论文，还有关于政治学和各种生物学问题，特别是动植物分类问题的论文。
Translation: Among them are papers on the logic and psychology he developed, as well as on political science and various biological issues, particularly those concerning the classification of animals and plants.

Query_Text_cn: 但是，尽管亚里斯多德在所有这些领域中都做出了巨大的贡献，并在死后影响了人类的思想达两千年之久，他在物理学领域中最重要的贡献也许只是创造了这门学科的名字，这是他从希腊字自然一词推演而来的。
Translation: However, despite Aristotle's tremendous contributions in all these fields and his influence on human thought for two thousand years after his death, perhaps his most significant contribution to the field of physics was merely coining the name of the discipline itself, which he derived from the Greek word for "nature."

Query_Text_cn: 亚里斯多德哲学对于研究物理学现象是不足的，这是因为他的哲学思想没有象许多其他古希腊哲学家那样与数学结合起来。
Translation: Aristotle's philosophy is inadequate for studying physical phenomena because, unlike many other ancient Greek philosophers, his philosophical thought was not integrated with mathematics.

Query_Text_cn: 他关于地上物运动的思想对科学进步所起作用几乎是害大于益。
Translation: His ideas on the motion of terrestrial objects have, in fact, done more harm than good to scientific progress.

Query_Text_cn: 到了文艺复兴时期科学思想再度活跃起来时，伽利略为了挣脱亚里斯多德哲学的羁绊而进行艰苦的斗争，因为当时公认亚里斯多德的思想是“知识的权威性结论”，完全不必去进一步探讨事物的本质了。
Translation: During the Renaissance, when scientific thought became active once again, Galileo engaged in a strenuous struggle to break free from the constraints of Aristotelian philosophy. At that time, Aristotle's ideas were widely recognized as the "authoritative conclusions of knowledge," making any further exploration into the nature of things seem unnecessary.

Query_Text_cn: 他在数学方面最重要的工作，是发现了球体及其外接圆柱体的面积与体积间的关系。事实上，按照他本人的意愿，他的墓地就是用一个球内接于圆柱体作为标志的。
Translation: His most significant contribution to mathematics was the discovery of the relationship between the surface area and volume of a sphere and its circumscribing cylinder. In fact, in accordance with his own wishes, his tomb is marked by a sphere inscribed within a cylinder.

Query_Text_cn: 在他写的一本名为“数沙者”的书中，他提出了一种书写很大数字的方法，按位置不同赋于一列数中每个数字以不同的“序”，并用这种方法来解决却何写下地球那样大的一个球体中所包含的沙粒数目的问题。
Translation: In his book titled "The Sand Reckoner," he proposed a method for writing very large numbers by assigning different "orders" to each digit in a column based on its position. He used this method to address the problem of how to record the number of grains of sand contained in a sphere as large as the Earth.

Query_Text_cn: 阿基米德在其名著“论平面的平衡”（两卷本）一书中提出了杠杆定律，并讨论了如何求任一给定物体的重心问题。
Translation: In his renowned two-volume work "On the Equilibrium of Planes," Archimedes introduced the law of the lever and discussed the problem of determining the center of gravity of any given object.

Query_Text_cn: 今天的读者会感到阿基米德的著作体裁太累赘又冗长，在很多方面都与欧几里德的几何书的体裁类似。
Translation: Today's readers may find Archimedes' works overly cumbersome and lengthy in style, which in many respects resembles the format of Euclid's geometry books.

Query_Text_cn: 事实上，在阿基米德那个时代，希腊的数学几乎完全局限于几何学，代数是很晚以后由阿拉伯人发明的。
Translation: In fact, during Archimedes' time, Greek mathematics was almost entirely limited to geometry, while algebra was invented much later by the Arabs.

Query_Text_cn: 因此，数学领域和其它物理学分支中的各种证明当时都是用几何作图来完成的，而不是象我们现在这祥去解代数方程。
Translation: Therefore, various proofs in the field of mathematics and other branches of physics at that time were all carried out using geometric constructions, rather than by solving algebraic equations as we do today.

Query_Text_cn: 和欧几里德几何学——许多读者在学校学习它时都曾累得满头大汗———样，阿基米德表述“静力学”（即平衡问题）的考本定律的方法也是先提出一些“公设”，然后再从中推演出若干“定理”。
Translation: Just like Euclidean geometry—which left many readers sweating when they studied it in school—Archimedes formulated the fundamental laws of "statics" (i.e., problems of equilibrium) by first proposing a set of "axioms" and then deducing a number of "theorems" from them.

Query_Text_cn: 相同的重物放在相同的距离上就处于平衡状态;而相同的重物放在不同的距离上则不平衡，杠杆要朝着放在较远距离上的那个重物倾斜。
Translation: Identical weights placed at the same distance are in a state of balance; however, if identical weights are placed at different distances, the lever becomes unbalanced and tilts toward the weight positioned farther away.

Query_Text_cn: 当放在一定距离上的重物处于平衡时，如果在其中一个重物上加一点份量，它们就不平衡了，杠杆要向加了份量的那个重物―端倾斜。
Translation: When two weights placed at a certain distance are in balance, adding a small amount of weight to one of them will disrupt the equilibrium, causing the lever to tilt toward the side with the added weight.

Query_Text_cn: 同理，如果从其中一个重物取出一点份量，它们也不平衡，杠杆向没有取出份量的那个重物一边倾斜。
Translation: Similarly, if a small amount of weight is removed from one of the heavy objects, the balance will also be disrupted, and the lever will tilt toward the side with the weight that remains untouched.

Query_Text_cn: 全等的平面图形如果互相重叠地放在一起，则它们的重心也同样重合。
Translation: If congruent plane figures are placed on top of each other so that they overlap exactly, their centroids will also coincide.

Query_Text_cn: 如果图形是不相等的但是相似，则其重心也有相似的位置。
Translation: If the figures are not congruent but are similar, their centroids will also occupy corresponding similar positions.

Query_Text_cn: 所谓相似图形的有相似位置的点，我的意思是指如果过这些点分别到相等的角作直线，则它们与对应的边所成之角也是相等的。
Translation: The so-called corresponding points in similar figures refer to points such that, if lines are drawn from these points at equal angles, the angles formed between these lines and the corresponding sides are also equal.

Query_Text_cn: 如果处在一定距离上的两个重物处于平衡，则另外两个与它们相等的重物处于同样距离时也会处于平衡（这不是显然的吗？）。
Translation: If two heavy objects at a certain distance from each other are in equilibrium, then two other objects of equal mass placed at the same distance will also be in equilibrium (isn't this obvious?).

Query_Text_cn: 任何一个图形，如果沿同一方向其周边都是下凹的，其重心必在图形之内。
Translation: For any shape, if all its edges are concave in the same direction, its centroid must lie within the shape.

Query_Text_cn: 从这些公设出发，靠直接的逻辑论证可以推出十五条定理。
Translation: From these axioms, fifteen theorems can be derived through direct logical reasoning.

Query_Text_cn: 我们这里给出前五个定理，而略去它们的证明，同时引述第六条定理的严格证明，因为其中包括了基本的杠杆定律。
Translation: Here, we present the first five theorems without their proofs, while providing a rigorous proof for the sixth theorem, as it includes the fundamental law of the lever.

Query_Text_cn: 如果两个相等的重物没有共同的重心，则整体的重心是在它们重心的联线的中点上。
Translation: If two equal weights do not share a common center of gravity, the overall center of gravity lies at the midpoint of the line connecting their centers of gravity.

Query_Text_cn: 如果三个相等重物的重心处在一条直线上，并隔开相等的距离，则整个体系的重心与中间重物的重心重合。
Translation: If the centers of gravity of three equal weights are aligned in a straight line and separated by equal distances, then the center of gravity of the entire system coincides with that of the middle weight.

Query_Text_cn: 两重物平衡时，所处的距离与重量成反比。
Translation: When two objects are balanced, the distance at which they are placed is inversely proportional to their weight.

Query_Text_cn: 杠杆原理的发现和各种应用在古代引起了一场轰动，我们可以在普鲁塔奇的“玛塞勒斯生平”—书所作的描写中看到这种情形。玛塞勒斯是第二次罗马与迦太基战争中占领了锡拉丘兹的一位罗马将军，他对杀害阿基米德要负部分责任，当时阿基米德由于建造了灵巧的故争机械而对锡拉丘兹的城防做了很大的贡献。
Translation: The discovery of the principle of the lever and its various applications caused a sensation in ancient times, as can be seen in Plutarch's account in "The Life of Marcellus." Marcellus was a Roman general who captured Syracuse during the Second Punic War between Rome and Carthage. He was partly responsible for the death of Archimedes, who had made significant contributions to the city's defenses by constructing ingenious war machines.

Query_Text_cn: 海罗大为惊奇，要他把他的主张付诸实施，表演一下怎样用微小的力去移动很大的重物。
Translation: Hero was greatly astonished and asked him to put his theory into practice by demonstrating how to move a very heavy object with a very small force.

Query_Text_cn: 于是阿基米德决定用一艘皇家船队的三桅货船，这种船通常要用很多劳力在岸上拉纤才能靠岸。在船上乘有许多旅客并装满了普通的货物后，阿某米德就呆在离船一段距离的地方，安静地转动他手里的一套滑轮组，毫不费力地就把船向自己平稳地拉过来了，仿佛船在水中行驶一样。
Translation: So Archimedes decided to use a three-masted cargo ship from the royal fleet, a type of vessel that usually required many laborers on shore to tow it to the dock. After the ship was loaded with many passengers and ordinary cargo, Archimedes stood some distance away from the vessel and quietly operated a set of pulleys in his hand. With hardly any effort, he steadily pulled the ship toward himself, as if the ship were gliding through the water.

Query_Text_cn: 杠杆原理在生活的各方面都起着十分重要的作用，从农民用撬棍移开重石直到现代工程技术中使用的错综复杂的机械都要用到它。
Translation: The principle of leverage plays a crucial role in all aspects of life, from farmers using crowbars to move heavy stones to the complex machinery employed in modern engineering.

Query_Text_cn: 阿基米德所提出的杠杆定律，使我们有可能引入作用力做功这样一个十分重要的力学概念。
Translation: The lever law proposed by Archimedes makes it possible for us to introduce the important mechanical concept of force doing work.

Query_Text_cn: 阿基米德所完成的一个最著名的发现，大概就是他的关于浸人液体中的物体失重的定律了。
Translation: One of Archimedes' most famous discoveries is probably his principle regarding the loss of weight of an object immersed in a liquid.

Query_Text_cn: “说起阿基米德，虽然他有许多各种各样的奇妙发现，可是在这所有的发现当中，我下面将要谈到的一个也许是最巧妙的了。
Translation: Speaking of Archimedes, although he made many remarkable discoveries, among all of them, the one I am about to discuss may be the most ingenious.

Query_Text_cn: 海罗在锡拉丘兹称王之后，为了显示自己的丰功伟绩，决定在一座圣庙里放上一顶金皇冠，奉献给不朽的神灵。
Translation: After becoming king in Syracuse, Hiero decided to place a golden crown in a temple as an offering to the immortal gods, in order to display his great achievements.

Query_Text_cn: 海罗与承包商谈好价钱，订了合间，并精确地称出黄金交给了他。
Translation: Hai Luo negotiated the price with the contractor, signed the contract, and precisely weighed out the gold to hand over to him.

Query_Text_cn: 到了规定的日期，制造商送来了做工极其精美的皇冠，大王极为满意。看起来皇冠的重量与所给的黄金重量完全相符。
Translation: On the appointed date, the manufacturer delivered an exquisitely crafted crown, which greatly pleased the king. The crown appeared to weigh exactly the same as the amount of gold provided.

Query_Text_cn: 但后来有人告发说，在做皇冠时,商人盗窃了金子，加上了等量的白银。
Translation: However, someone later reported that when making the crown, the merchant stole some gold and added an equal amount of silver.

Query_Text_cn: 海罗认为自己受了欺骗，实在是奇耻大辱，但又没有办法把窃贼的嘴脸揭露出来，就命阿基米德想想办法。
Translation: Hero felt deeply humiliated by the deception but had no way to expose the thief's true nature, so he ordered Archimedes to find a solution.

Query_Text_cn: 以此作为其发现的开端，据说他做了两件重量与皇冠相同的物体,一件是黄金的，另一件是白银的。
Translation: Taking this as the starting point of his discovery, it is said that he made two objects of the same weight as the crown, one of gold and the other of silver.

Query_Text_cn: 做好之后，他把一个大容器用水装得满满的，并把银制品放了进去。
Translation: After finishing, he filled a large container with water and placed the silverware inside.

Query_Text_cn: 溢出来的水的体积与沉人容器中的白银体积是相等的。
Translation: The volume of the water that overflows is equal to the volume of the silver submerged in the container.

Query_Text_cn: 然后他把物体取出来，用量杯把水注入容器，以补偿溢出的水，直到恢复原来的满度。
Translation: He then took out the object and used a measuring cup to pour water into the container to compensate for the overflowed water until it returned to its original full level.

Query_Text_cn: 这样他就求出了与确定量的水相对应的银子的体积。
Translation: In this way, he calculated the volume of silver corresponding to a specific quantity of water.

Query_Text_cn: 做完这个实验后,他又把金制品放入装满了水的容器中，然后取出来，照上次一样用量杯把水装满，他发现这次溢出的水没有上次那么多，稍微少了一点儿。也就是说，金子的体积比相同重量的银子的体积小多少，水也正好少多少。
Translation: After completing this experiment, he placed the gold object into a container filled with water, then took it out and, as before, refilled the container to the brim with a measuring cup. He found that this time, the amount of water that overflowed was slightly less than the previous time. In other words, the volume of gold is exactly as much less than that of silver of the same weight as the difference in the amount of water displaced.

Query_Text_cn: 最后，他又用水装满容器,并把皇冠放进同样多量的水中，发现皇冠排出的水比同样重的金制品排出的水要多。
Translation: Finally, he filled the container with water again and placed the crown into the same amount of water, discovering that the crown displaced more water than a gold object of equal weight.

Query_Text_cn: 因此，他基于这一事实证明了金里掺进了白银，把制造商这个窃贼的嘴脸暴露在光天化日之下了。
Translation: Therefore, based on this fact, he proved that gold had been adulterated with silver, thereby exposing the manufacturer as a thief in broad daylight.

Query_Text_cn: 他在“论浮体”一书中给出的阿基米德定律的证明虽然完全正确，但是有点繁琐。这里我们把它用现代的语言复述一下。试考虑我们把一个固体金属球放人水槽屮所会发生的情况。
Translation: Although his proof of Archimedes' principle in the book "On Floating Bodies" is entirely correct, it is somewhat cumbersome. Here, we restate it in modern language. Consider what happens when we place a solid metal sphere into a water tank.

Query_Text_cn: 假定我们先不用铁球，而用一个直径与铁球相间的充满水的薄塑料球。
Translation: Suppose we use a thin plastic ball filled with water, with a diameter alternating with that of the iron ball, instead of the iron ball for now.

Query_Text_cn: 因为塑料球壳的重量可以忽略不计，这种情况就好象球壳中的水正好就是槽中水的一部分，所以刻度器上的指示将为零。
Translation: Because the weight of the plastic sphere shell can be neglected, it is as if the water inside the sphere shell is simply part of the water in the trough, so the reading on the gauge will be zero.

Query_Text_cn: 现在用铁来置换球壳中的水，铁的重量是同体积的水的七倍，因为一磅的水被槽中其余的水支撑时刻度器的指示是零，所以用铁置换水时只会增加7—1=6磅，那也就是这种情况下刻度器上的读数。
Translation: Now, iron is used to replace the water in the spherical shell. The weight of iron is seven times that of water of the same volume. Since the scale reads zero when one pound of water is supported by the rest of the water in the tank, replacing the water with iron will only increase the weight by 7-1=6 pounds, which will be the reading on the scale in this case.

Query_Text_cn: 由此可以得出结论，在空气中重七磅的铁球，由于浸没在水中而失去了一磅的重量，这也就是它所排开的水的重量。
Translation: It can thus be concluded that an iron ball weighing seven pounds in air loses one pound of its weight when submerged in water, which is exactly the weight of the water it displaces.

Query_Text_cn: 这就是阿基米德定律，即任何固态物体浸入液体中所失去的重量，等于它排除的液体的重量。
Translation: This is Archimedes' principle, which states that any solid object immersed in a liquid loses an amount of weight equal to the weight of the liquid it displaces.

Query_Text_cn: 阿基米德不仅是一位伟大的数学家和力学的奠基人，而且用现代的语言来说，他还是一位“工业和武装力量的顾问”在他的工程发明中，最著名的就是所谓“阿基米德螺旋”，如图1-7所示，它是用来提升水的。
Translation: Archimedes was not only a great mathematician and a founder of mechanics, but, in modern terms, he was also an "industrial and military consultant." Among his engineering inventions, the most famous is the so-called "Archimedes' screw," as shown in Figure 1-7, which was used to lift water.

Query_Text_cn: 这种装置及其作用是不言自明的，它被广泛地用于灌溉和从矿井中抽出地下水。
Translation: The function of this device is self-evident; it is widely used for irrigation and for pumping groundwater from mines.

Query_Text_cn: 阿基米德参与军事工作显然是从他给海罗大王演示滑轮实验时开始的。
Translation: Archimedes' involvement in military affairs clearly began when he demonstrated the pulley experiment to King Hiero.

Query_Text_cn: “海罗对阿基米德的表演感到惊奇并理解了这一技巧的功效，于是，他说服阿基米德为他准备一些攻击和防守的机械，以用于任何一种攻城战。
Translation: Hero was amazed by Archimedes' demonstration and understood the effectiveness of the technique. Consequently, he persuaded Archimedes to prepare some offensive and defensive machines for him, to be used in any kind of siege warfare.

Query_Text_cn: 这些东西他本人从来没有用过，因为他的大半生都是在没有故争以及和平的喜庆典礼中渡过的，但现在这些器械以及它们的制造者却给锡位丘兹人带来了很大的益处。
Translation: He himself had never used these items, as he spent most of his life in times without conflict and in the joyful ceremonies of peace. However, these tools and their makers have now brought great benefits to the people of Xiwaiqiuz.

Query_Text_cn: 当罗马人从海上和陆地向锡拉丘兹人进攻时，锡拉丘玆人全被吓呆了，觉得简直毫无办法来抵挡罗马人如此可怕的攻击。
Translation: When the Romans attacked the Syracusans from both sea and land, the people of Syracuse were utterly terrified and felt completely helpless to resist such a formidable assault from the Romans.

Query_Text_cn: 但这时阿基米德开始使用了他的机械，他向陆上进攻的敌人射出了各种飞弹和大量巨石，它们以惊人的速度呼啸着倾盆而下,敌兵根本无法招架，一堆堆地被打倒在地，队列也被打得七零八落。
Translation: At this moment, Archimedes began to employ his machines, launching various projectiles and massive stones at the enemy forces advancing on land. These missiles hurtled down with astonishing speed and force, leaving the enemy utterly unable to withstand them. Soldiers fell in heaps, and their formations were shattered and thrown into disarray.

Query_Text_cn: 同时，巨大的木梁突然从城墙射到敌船上，沉重的重物从髙处掉下来，击沉了一部分船只，其余的则被铁爪或类似起重机铁嘴似的铁钩抓住船头，直吊上空中，而船尾朝下陷进深水，或被城里的机械搞得团闭转，被城墙下面凸出的悬崖峭壁撞得粉碎，给失事船上的战斗人员造成极大的伤亡。
Translation: Meanwhile, massive wooden beams were suddenly launched from the city walls onto the enemy ships, and heavy objects were dropped from above, sinking some of the vessels. The remaining ships were seized at the bow by iron claws or crane-like iron hooks, hoisted high into the air, with their sterns plunging downward into deep water. Others were ensnared by city machinery, spun around in confusion, and smashed to pieces against the protruding cliffs beneath the city walls, causing heavy casualties among the combatants on the stricken ships.

Query_Text_cn: 而且，战船往往会离开水面，被举到半空，忽东忽西地乱转，就象被悬挂起来一样，形成一幅极其可怕的景象，直到仝体船员向四面八方被抛出去，这时空船就会落到城墙上，或者脱开抓住它的铁钩掉下水去。
Translation: Moreover, the warships would often be lifted out of the water and suspended in midair, spinning erratically from east to west as if they were hanging, creating an extremely terrifying scene. This would continue until the entire crew was thrown in all directions, at which point the empty ship would either fall onto the city wall or break free from the iron hooks holding it and plunge back into the water.

Query_Text_cn: 至于玛塞勒斯自己带到船桥上的机械（这种机械因为有点象一种叫做塞姆布卡的乐器，所以被称为“塞姆布卡”。），当它到城墙还有一定距离的时侯，一块十泰伦重的石头就射到它上面，接着又是第二块，第三块，有些石头带着巨大的声响砸过来，摧毁了机械的基础，使其粉身碎骨，从台架上垮下来，搞得玛塞勒斯狼狈不堪，不得不下令让他的船队尽快返航，而他的陆上军队也只好撤退了。
Translation: As for the machine that Marcellus himself brought onto the ship bridge (this machine was called the "Sambuca" because it somewhat resembled a musical instrument of the same name), when it was still some distance from the city walls, a ten-talent stone was hurled at it, followed by a second and a third. Some of these stones crashed down with tremendous noise, destroying the foundation of the machine, shattering it to pieces, and causing it to collapse from its platform. Marcellus was thrown into confusion and had no choice but to order his fleet to retreat as quickly as possible, while his land forces were also forced to withdraw.

Query_Text_cn: 后来，在一次军事会议上，罗马人决定，如有可能，就先在夜间到达城下，他们以为既然阿基米德在他的机械中所用的绳子能给飞石以巨大的推动力，它们也就可能使飞石从他们头顶上方飞过去，而不会在近处发挥作用，因近处没有可供投射的空间。
Translation: Later, at a military meeting, the Romans decided that, if possible, they would arrive at the city walls during the night. They believed that since the ropes used in Archimedes' machines could impart tremendous force to the projectiles, the stones might fly over their heads rather than exert their effect at close range, as there was no space nearby for launching them.

Query_Text_cn: 但是，阿基米徳似乎早就准备好对付这种紧急情况的机械了，它们适用于任何距离和短程发射，通过城墙上接连开出的许多小孔，这些称为“投石机”的近程机械能瞄准近处目标而不被敌人发觉。
Translation: However, Archimedes seemed to have long been prepared for such emergencies with machines suitable for any distance and short-range launches. Through numerous small openings created along the city walls, these short-range devices, known as "catapults," could target nearby enemies without being detected.

Query_Text_cn: 所以，当罗马人到达城下以为自己没有被发现时，就再次遇到了暴风雨般的飞石，巨大的石块几乎笔直地向他们砸下来，墙上各处都向他们射出利箭，于是他们又败退了。
Translation: Therefore, when the Romans arrived at the city walls, believing they had not been detected, they were once again met with a storm of flying stones. Huge rocks rained down almost vertically upon them, and sharp arrows were shot at them from all parts of the wall, forcing them to retreat once more.

Query_Text_cn: 接着，当他们退开一定距离时，飞石又飞上前来落到他们头上，许多船只也互相撞毁了。他们根本无法报复自己的敌人，因为阿基米德把他的机械大部分建造在紧靠城墙背后，罗马人好象是在跟神灵打仗一样，所以无数的灾难从看不见的地方倾注在他们头上。
Translation: Then, as they retreated a certain distance, stones would fly forward again and fall upon their heads, and many ships were also smashed against each other. They were completely unable to retaliate against their enemies, because Archimedes had constructed most of his machines just behind the city walls. It was as if the Romans were fighting against the gods, with countless disasters raining down upon them from unseen places.

Query_Text_cn: 玛塞勒斯逃跑了，他对自己的工匠和工程师们戏谑地说：“算了吧,跟这位几何学的百手巨人打仗时，他拿咱们的舰队象酒杯一样从海里舀水，咱们自己的塞姆布卡又这么不光彩地让他搞得一塌糊涂，他一下子就向咱们全体射来了那么多的石弹，真比神话里的白手妖怪还要厉害。
Translation: Marcellus fled and jokingly said to his craftsmen and engineers, "Forget it. When fighting this hundred-handed giant of geometry, he scoops up our fleet from the sea as if they were wine cups. Our own sambuca was so disgracefully ruined by him, and he fired so many stones at all of us at once—he's even more formidable than the legendary white-handed monster."

Query_Text_cn: 实际上，锡拉丘兹的全体居民已成为阿基米德的设计整体，他一个人主宰和运筹着一切，其它的武器都闲置不用了，当时攻城守城都只用他的机械。
Translation: In fact, all the inhabitants of Syracuse had become part of Archimedes’ grand design; he alone directed and managed everything, while all other weapons were left unused. At that time, both the offense and defense of the city relied solely on his machines.

Query_Text_cn: 最后,罗马人变得如此神经过敏，任何时候只要看见城墙里伸出一小节绳子或一根小木棍，他们也会大喊起来：“又是它！阿基米德又在弄什么新玩艺儿打咱们了！”接着就转身赶快逃炮。
Translation: In the end, the Romans became so jittery that whenever they saw even a small piece of rope or a stick protruding from the city walls, they would shout, "There it is again! What new contraption is Archimedes using against us now?" Then they would immediately turn and flee.

Query_Text_cn: 看到这些，玛塞勒斯只好打消攻打的念头，从此以后开始依靠长期的围困战术了。
Translation: Seeing this, Marcellus had no choice but to abandon the idea of launching an attack and, from then on, began to rely on prolonged siege tactics.

Query_Text_cn: 围城两年以后，公元前212年，锡拉丘兹终于被罗马军队占领了，一小队罗马士兵闯进了阿基米德的家，他正在后院忙着在沙子上画一些复杂的几何图形。
Translation: Two years after the siege, in 212 BC, Syracuse was finally captured by the Roman army. A small group of Roman soldiers broke into Archimedes' house while he was busy drawing complex geometric figures in the sand in his backyard.

Query_Text_cn: 这个大兵的回答是挥动他的长矛刺穿了这位老哲学家的身躯。
Translation: The soldier's response was to thrust his spear through the body of the old philosopher.

Query_Text_cn: 公元前137年，当西塞罗作为一位会计官访问西西里时，他在阿格里琴门附近发现了阿基米德墓，墓上长满了荆棘和野草。
Translation: In 137 BC, when Cicero visited Sicily as a quaestor, he discovered Archimedes' tomb near the Agrigentum Gate, which was overgrown with thorns and weeds.

Query_Text_cn: 西塞罗写道：“要不是有一位阿平宁的山民发现的话，这座最有名，而且一度是最文明的希腊城市，到现在也不会知道它最有天才的一位公民的坟墓在什么地方。
Translation: Cicero wrote, "If it had not been for a mountaineer from the Apennines, the most famous and once the most civilized Greek city would still not know the location of the tomb of its most gifted citizen."

Query_Text_cn: 随着雅典的政治与经济力量的衰落，希腊文化的中心逐渐转移到了亚历山大里亚，它是由亚历山大大帝于公元前332年在地中海的埃及海岸上建立起来的，是欧洲和东方之间的贸易枢纽。
Translation: With the decline of Athens' political and economic power, the center of Greek culture gradually shifted to Alexandria, which was founded by Alexander the Great in 332 BC on the Egyptian coast of the Mediterranean Sea and served as a trade hub between Europe and the East.

Query_Text_cn: 那时亚历山大里亚已经发展成一座美丽的城市，有“……4000座宫殿，4000个澡堂，12000名花匠，40000名纳贡的犹太人，400座剧场和其它娱乐场所。
Translation: At that time, Alexandria had already developed into a beautiful city, boasting "4,000 palaces, 4,000 bathhouses, 12,000 gardeners, 40,000 tribute-paying Jews, 400 theaters, and other entertainment venues."

Query_Text_cn: 它还有一所第一流的大学和一座庞大的图书馆。后来，由于凯撒下令烧掉亚历山大港的埃及舰队而引起全城大火，图书馆不幸被烧毁了。
Translation: It also had a first-class university and a vast library. Later, a citywide fire broke out after Caesar ordered the burning of the Egyptian fleet in Alexandria, and unfortunately, the library was destroyed in the blaze.

Query_Text_cn: 欧几里德曾在这里写了他的“几何学原本”，阿基米徳年青时也曾从锡拉丘兹到这里来学过科学知识。
Translation: Euclid once wrote his "Elements of Geometry" here, and Archimedes, in his youth, also came from Syracuse to study scientific knowledge.

Query_Text_cn: 在天文学方面，亚历山大里亚的代表人物是希伯楚斯。他生于公元前三世纪中叶。希伯楚斯以当时可能有的最高精度观察了星球的位置，编制了1080个星球的星表，至今天文学家还在使用它，作为有关行星位置的古代参考资料。
Translation: In astronomy, the representative figure of Alexandria was Hipparchus. He was born in the mid-third century BC. Hipparchus observed the positions of celestial bodies with the highest possible precision at the time and compiled a star catalog of 1,080 stars, which is still used by astronomers today as an ancient reference for planetary positions.

Query_Text_cn: 他还发现了岁差现象，即太阳在其周年运动中通过天球赤道时与其交点不断改变位置的现象。
Translation: He also discovered the phenomenon of precession, which refers to the continuous change in the position of the intersection points where the Sun crosses the celestial equator during its annual motion.

Query_Text_cn: 这种现象的产生是由于地球的自转轴与其轨道平面成一倾斜角，自转轴将绕着垂直于轨道平面的直线在空间扫出一个锥体，其周期是26000年。
Translation: This phenomenon arises because the Earth's axis of rotation is tilted relative to its orbital plane. The rotational axis traces out a cone in space around a line perpendicular to the orbital plane, with a period of 26,000 years.

Query_Text_cn: 产生这种运动的原因则几乎在一千年后才被牛顿发现。
Translation: The cause of this motion was not discovered until nearly a thousand years later by Newton.

Query_Text_cn: 至于物理学方面，亚历山大学派的代表人物是赫伦与其说他是一位物理学家，倒不如说他是一位工程发明家更为合适。
Translation: As for the field of physics, the representative figure of the Alexandrian school is Heron. Rather than calling him a physicist, it would be more appropriate to describe him as an engineering inventor.

Query_Text_cn: 他的“力学”一书中有许多正确的陈述，但也有不少糟糕的数学错误。
Translation: His book "Mechanics" contains many accurate statements, but also quite a few serious mathematical errors.

Query_Text_cn: 虽然赫伦论述力学的书中在基本问题的数学处理上有缺点，但书中也描述了大量有用的机件，诸如滑轮组，各种传动装置和齿轮机构等等。
Translation: Although Heron's treatise on mechanics has shortcomings in the mathematical treatment of fundamental problems, it also describes a large number of useful mechanical devices, such as pulley systems, various transmission mechanisms, and gear assemblies.

Query_Text_cn: 在其“汽力学”一书中，他描述了虹吸原理和蒸汽喷气机，这种喷气机类似普通的草地喷水壶，但可以看成是现代喷汽发动机的先驱。
Translation: In his book "Pneumatics," he described the principle of the siphon and the steam jet engine, which was similar to an ordinary lawn sprinkler but can be regarded as the precursor to the modern jet engine.

Query_Text_cn: 赫伦还写过一本名为《反射光学》的书，其内容是关于镜子的理论及其实际应用。
Translation: Heron also wrote a book titled "Catoptrics," which deals with the theory of mirrors and their practical applications.

Query_Text_cn: “反射光学显然是一门科学，值得加以研究，它可以产生使观察者感到惊奇的景象。
Translation: Reflective optics is clearly a science worthy of study, as it can produce phenomena that astonish observers.

Query_Text_cn: 因为借助这门科学，我们可以做成一些镜子，把右边照成右边，同样把左边也照成左边，而普通的镜子本来是有相反特性的，即照出相反的一边。
Translation: With the help of this science, we can create mirrors that reflect the right side as the right side and the left side as the left side, whereas ordinary mirrors have the opposite property—they reflect the opposite side.

Query_Text_cn: 把两面没有框架的镜子的边缘连接并相互成直角地放在一起，就可以做到这一点。
Translation: This can be achieved by joining the edges of two frameless mirrors and placing them together at a right angle.

Query_Text_cn: “借助镜子，我们能够看到自己的背后（理发师给你看颈后的发型就是这样），也能看到自己倒过来，头朝下，有三只眼腈和两个鼻子，好象处干极度悲痛之中那样面孔发生畸变（象游艺场镜馆里的情形那样）。
Translation: With the help of a mirror, we can see the back of our own heads (just as a barber shows you the hairstyle at the nape of your neck), or see ourselves upside down, with three eyes and two noses, our faces grotesquely distorted as if in extreme grief (like what happens in a funhouse of mirrors).

Query_Text_cn: “实际上，所有写过屈光学问题的人都有疑问，为什么从我们眼里发出的光线会被镜子反射，为什么又以相等的角度反射。
Translation: In fact, everyone who has written about the problems of optics has wondered why the rays of light emitted from our eyes are reflected by a mirror, and why they are reflected at equal angles.

Query_Text_cn: 我们的视线从视觉器官发出时是沿着直线进行的，这个命题现在可以证实如下。
Translation: The proposition that our line of sight travels in a straight line from the visual organ can now be confirmed as follows.

Query_Text_cn: 因为任何以不变速度运动的东西都是沿直线运动的。
Translation: Because anything moving at a constant speed always travels in a straight line.

Query_Text_cn: 我们看到弓上射出的箭，可以做为一个例子。
Translation: We can take the arrow shot from a bow as an example.

Query_Text_cn: 由于推力，箭在运动中力求走过尽可能短的距离，因为它没有时间使运动变慢，就是说，没有时间走过更长的轨道，推力不允许有这样的耽搁。
Translation: Due to thrust, the arrow strives to travel the shortest possible distance during its motion, because it does not have time to slow down—in other words, it does not have time to follow a longer trajectory. The thrust does not permit such delays.

Query_Text_cn: 所以，由于箭的速度，它倾向于走最短的路径。
Translation: Therefore, due to the speed of the arrow, it tends to follow the shortest path.

Query_Text_cn: 伹是，在所有有相同终始端的线中，最短的就是直线。
Translation: However, among all lines with the same endpoints, the shortest one is the straight line.

Query_Text_cn: 从下面的考虑就可了解我们眼中所发出的光线是以无穷大的速度运动的，当我们闭上眼睛后再睁开来观看天空时，并不需要什么时间视线就到达天空了。
Translation: From the following consideration, it becomes clear that the light emitted from our eyes travels at an infinite speed. When we close our eyes and then open them to look at the sky, it takes no time at all for our line of sight to reach the sky.

Query_Text_cn: 确实，尽管星星的距离可以说是无限远，当我们去看它们时立刻就看到了。
Translation: Indeed, although the stars may be said to be infinitely distant, we see them instantly when we look at them.

Query_Text_cn: 而且，如果星星的距离再增大，结果还是一样，所以，光线显然是以无限大的速度射出的。
Translation: Moreover, if the distance between the stars increases further, the result remains the same; therefore, it is evident that light is emitted at an infinite speed.

Query_Text_cn: 因此，它们若不受阻碍或被弯曲，总是沿最短的路径即直线运动。
Translation: Therefore, if they are not obstructed or deflected, they will always move along the shortest path, that is, in a straight line.

Query_Text_cn: 这段话揭示了一个可笑的事实，即赫伦和他所有同时代的人都以为视觉的产生是由于眼睛发出了某种射线被物体反射回来，今天的雷达所依据的正是这个原理。
Translation: This passage reveals a ridiculous fact: Heron and all his contemporaries believed that vision was produced by rays emitted from the eyes and reflected back by objects—a principle that modern radar is based on.

Query_Text_cn: 亚历山大里亚的另一位伟大人物是克劳迪亚斯·托勒密（不要和托勒密王朝的人混淆了）。他生活在公元二世纪的前半期。托勒密对恒星和行屋的观察，都收集在他的一本名为《伟大论》的书中，对希伯楚斯早在两个半世纪之前所得到的资料做了相当可观的补充。
Translation: Another great figure from Alexandria was Claudius Ptolemy (not to be confused with members of the Ptolemaic dynasty). He lived during the first half of the second century AD. Ptolemy's observations of stars and planets were compiled in his book titled "The Almagest," which provided substantial additions to the data obtained by Hipparchus more than two and a half centuries earlier.

Query_Text_cn: 他对物理学的重要贡献包括在其《光学》一书中，我们今天见到的是从佚散的阿拉伯文译本转译的拉丁文译本，而阿拉伯文本是从希腊文手稿译出的。
Translation: His significant contributions to physics include his work "Optics," which we know today through a Latin translation derived from a lost Arabic version, itself translated from a Greek manuscript.

Query_Text_cn: 托勒密在这本书里讨论了许多问题，其中包括光从一种介质进入另一种介质时发生折射这个重要的课题。
Translation: In this book, Ptolemy discusses a variety of issues, including the important topic of the refraction of light as it passes from one medium into another.

Query_Text_cn: “可见光可以有两种方式改变路径：一是被反射，即被物体反弹回来，这种物体称为镜子，光线不能穿透；一是在介质中被弯曲（即折射），这时光线能穿透介质，这种介质有一个共同的名称（透明物质），因为可见光线能够穿透它们。
Translation: Visible light can change its path in two ways: first, by being reflected, that is, bounced back by an object. Such objects are called mirrors, and light cannot penetrate them. Second, by being bent within a medium (that is, refracted), in which case light can pass through the medium. These media share a common name—transparent materials—because visible light is able to penetrate them.

Query_Text_cn: 托勒密用下面一个简单的实验说明了折射现象：把一枚硬币放在一只装满水的称为“洗礼盆”的容器底部。
Translation: Ptolemy illustrated the phenomenon of refraction with a simple experiment: he placed a coin at the bottom of a vessel filled with water, known as a "baptismal font."

Query_Text_cn: “假定眼睛的位置使得它所发射的可见光线刚好通过洗礼盆的边缘到达比硬币略高的地点。
Translation: Assume that the position of the eye allows the emitted visible light to pass just over the edge of the baptismal font and reach a point slightly higher than the coin.

Query_Text_cn: 然后让硬币保持原地不动，慢慢向盆里注水，直到从盆边射过去的光线向下弯曲刚好落到硬币上为止。
Translation: Then keep the coin stationary and slowly pour water into the basin until the light beam projected from the edge of the basin bends downward and just falls on the coin.

Query_Text_cn: 结果是，原来看不到的物体现在顺着从眼睛通到物体真正位置上方一点的直线可以看到了。
Translation: As a result, objects that were previously invisible can now be seen along a straight line extending from the eye to a point just above the object's actual position.

Query_Text_cn: 但观察者不会假定视线已经弯向物体，而会认为物体自行浮了起来，向视线方向升高了。
Translation: However, the observer does not assume that the line of sight has bent toward the object, but rather believes that the object itself has floated up and risen in the direction of the line of sight.

Query_Text_cn: 因此，物体将会出现在从它向水面所作的垂直线上。
Translation: Therefore, the object will appear on the vertical line drawn from it to the water surface.

Query_Text_cn: 托勒密后来在书中又描述了一个实验，想仔细研究一下光的折射定律。
Translation: Ptolemy later described another experiment in his book, aiming to study the law of refraction of light in detail.

Query_Text_cn: 托勒密还用类似的方法研究了光线在空气和玻璃的交界面上的折射，并发现在这种情况下光线的弯曲更大。
Translation: Ptolemy also used a similar method to study the refraction of light at the interface between air and glass, and found that in this case the bending of light was even greater.

Query_Text_cn: 但是，托勒密没有试图（或者是做过，但至少是没有取得成功）用数学公式把他的观察结果表达出来。表达光的折射定律的数学公式直到十七世纪才被发现。
Translation: However, Ptolemy did not attempt (or at least did not succeed) to express his observations using mathematical formulas. The mathematical expression of the law of refraction of light was not discovered until the seventeenth century.

Query_Text_cn: 颇具讽刺意味的是，他本来可以轻而易举地做到这一点，因为用公式表达这个定律所需要的数学工具乃是弧度和弦长之问的关系，而这早在他一个半世纪以前就已由普鲁塔奇研究过了，托勒密本人在《伟大论》屮谈到天文观测时也用很大篇幅阐述了这一关系。
Translation: Ironically, he could have accomplished this with ease, as the mathematical tool required to express this law in formulaic terms—the relationship between radians and chord length—had already been studied by Plutarch a century and a half earlier. Ptolemy himself devoted considerable space to explaining this relationship in his Almagest when discussing astronomical observations.

Query_Text_cn: 问题是要求出具有单位半径的圆中弧ACB所对应的弦长ADB。
Translation: The problem is to find the length of chord ADB corresponding to arc ACB in a circle with unit radius.

Query_Text_cn: 托勒密用很巧妙的数学方法编制了一个表，下面摘录其中的一部分。
Translation: Ptolemy devised a table using ingenious mathematical methods, and a portion of it is excerpted below.

Query_Text_cn: 这个表相当于现在所说的正弦三角函数表，唯一的区别在于现在是用半长（即角AOC）和半弦长AD。
Translation: This table is equivalent to what is now known as a table of sine trigonometric functions, with the only difference being that it uses the half-chord (i.e., angle AOC) and the half-chord length AD.

Query_Text_cn: 在单位圆情况下，长度AD称为角AOC的正弦，长度OD则称为角AOC的余弦。
Translation: In the case of the unit circle, the length AD is called the sine of angle AOC, and the length OD is called the cosine of angle AOC.

Query_Text_cn: 三角函數在解决既包括长度又包括角度的几何问题时是极为有用的。
Translation: Trigonometric functions are extremely useful in solving geometric problems that involve both lengths and angles.

Query_Text_cn: 如果托勒密把他关于光折射的实验结果与他的正弦表作一比较的话，他就会发入射角的正弦与折射角的正弦之比对给定的两种介质来说是一个常数。
Translation: If Ptolemy had compared the results of his experiments on light refraction with his table of sines, he would have found that the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is a constant for any given pair of media.

Query_Text_cn: 他没有这样做，结果这个折射定律一直没有被发现，直到十四个世纪以后，它才由荷兰的天文学家和数学家斯奈尔发现。
Translation: He did not do so, and as a result, the law of refraction remained undiscovered until fourteen centuries later, when it was finally discovered by Dutch astronomer and mathematician Snell.

Query_Text_cn: 以后我们将看到，斯奈尔定律对理解光的本性是有着极其重要的意义的。
Translation: As we will see later, Snell's law is of great significance for understanding the nature of light.

Query_Text_cn: 托勒密的工作是古希腊文化对科学发展的最后一个伟大贡献。在他死后，亚历山大学派的科学研究很快就开始衰落了。
Translation: Ptolemy's work was the last great contribution of ancient Greek culture to the development of science. After his death, scientific research at the Alexandrian school quickly began to decline.

Query_Text_cn: 与亚历山大学派有关的中的人物中，最后一个值得一提的名字也许是海帕蒂，她是数学家西恩的女儿，是一位科学和哲学教师。
Translation: The last notable figure associated with the Alexandrian school is perhaps Hypatia, the daughter of the mathematician Theon, who was a teacher of science and philosophy.

Query_Text_cn: 她生于罗马朱理安帝国统治时期，朱理安曾力图保护希腊文化和希腊神的偶像，使之不受力量日益增长的基督教的侵犯。
Translation: She was born during the reign of the Julian emperors in Rome, a period when Julian made great efforts to protect Greek culture and the idols of Greek gods from the encroachment of the increasingly powerful Christianity.

Query_Text_cn: 朱理安死后出现的复古运动引起了公元415年由亚历山大里亚的克瑞勒主教所组织的反希腊大暴动。
Translation: The revivalist movement that emerged after Julian's death triggered an anti-Greek riot in 415 AD, organized by Cyril, the Bishop of Alexandria.

Query_Text_cn: 海帕蒂被基督教暴徒撕成了碎片，这个城市的图书馆遗迹也都被毁了。
Translation: Hypatia was torn to pieces by Christian mobs, and the remnants of the city's library were also destroyed.

Query_Text_cn: 随着希腊文化的毁灭，一般科学，特别是物理学的发展完全停顿了。
Translation: With the destruction of Greek culture, the development of general science, especially physics, came to a complete halt.

Query_Text_cn: 在人类历史的这一段时期曾经统治过世界的罗马人对抽象思考很少关心，他们的文化成了“实业家文化”。尽管他们也鼓励研究学问，但主要是对实用问题感兴趣。
Translation: During this period of human history, the Romans, who once ruled the world, showed little interest in abstract thinking. Their culture became a "culture of practical enterprise." Although they also encouraged the pursuit of knowledge, their main interest lay in practical matters.

Query_Text_cn: 罗马帝国衰亡之后，情况更是糟糕，在帝国的废墟上建立起来的封建国家当然也不是任何科学发展的沃土。
Translation: After the fall of the Roman Empire, the situation worsened. The feudal states that arose from the ruins of the empire were certainly not fertile ground for any scientific development.

Query_Text_cn: 在这整整一千多年的漫长时期中，唯一统一的刺激品就是基督教，大寺、教堂和修道院成了文化的中心。
Translation: Throughout this long period of more than a thousand years, the only unifying stimulus was Christianity, with cathedrals, churches, and monasteries becoming the centers of culture.

Query_Text_cn: 因此，当时主要的兴趣是集中在理性问题上，古希腊文化衰落后遗留下来的不管什么科学思想都屈服于宗教的专政之下。
Translation: Therefore, the main interest at that time was focused on issues of rationality, and any scientific thought left behind after the decline of ancient Greek culture was subordinated to the autocracy of religion.

Query_Text_cn: 托勒密的天动说——即认为地球在中心是静止的，而太阳、行星和运动的理论，被公认为不可动摇的信条。因为这种理论最适合于挑选的使者所居住的地方。
Translation: The Ptolemaic geocentric theory—which holds that the Earth is stationary at the center while the Sun, planets, and stars move around it—was universally regarded as an unshakable doctrine, as this theory was best suited to the place inhabited by the chosen messengers.

Query_Text_cn: “科学”讨论都被局限在诸如一个针尖上能有多少个天使在跳舞以及上帝是否能造出一块他自己也举不起来的大石头之类的问题。
Translation: "Scientific" discussions have been confined to questions such as how many angels can dance on the head of a pin and whether God can create a stone so heavy that even He cannot lift it.

Query_Text_cn: 原始的“李森科主义”席卷了整个欧洲，神圣的宗教裁判所无情镇压着任何背离宗教信仰的思想。
Translation: The original "Lysenkoism" swept across Europe, and the Holy Inquisition ruthlessly suppressed any ideas that deviated from religious beliefs.

Query_Text_cn: 对我们来说幸运的是，希腊科学在公元七世纪期间新生的阿拉伯帝国找到了避难所，帝国并吞了地中海整个南部的土地，直到狭窄的直布罗陀海峡对岸的西班牙。
Translation: Fortunately for us, Greek science found refuge in the newly established Arab Empire during the seventh century AD. The empire annexed the entire southern Mediterranean region, reaching as far as Spain across the narrow Strait of Gibraltar.

Query_Text_cn: “一千零一夜”故事中的仁慈的君主哈伦·阿尔拉齐德于公元800年在巴格达建立了一所科学学校，同时，西班牙的科尔瓦多市也成了阿拉伯帝国在欧洲土地上的文化中心。
Translation: The benevolent monarch Harun al-Rashid from the tales of "One Thousand and One Nights" established a scientific academy in Baghdad in the year 800. At the same time, the city of Cordoba in Spain also became the cultural center of the Arab Empire on European soil.

Query_Text_cn: 阿拉伯学者们研究和翻译了从部分被毁的希腊人图书馆中抢救出来的希腊手稿，举起了科学的旗帜，而当时的欧洲正被窒息在中世纪经院哲学的桎梏之中。
Translation: Arab scholars studied and translated Greek manuscripts salvaged from partially destroyed Greek libraries, raising the banner of science at a time when Europe was suffocating under the shackles of medieval scholasticism.

Query_Text_cn: 科学史上的阿拉伯时代，可以由一些延用至今的科学名词得到证明，诸如代数、酒精、碱、汞、合金、日历等等。
Translation: The Arab era in the history of science can be evidenced by several scientific terms still in use today, such as algebra, alcohol, alkali, mercury, alloy, calendar, and so on.

Query_Text_cn: 阿拉伯人在数学方面有了长足进步，发展了希腊人所不知道的代数学，引进了阿拉伯数字，使得计算比用罗马制方便多了。
Translation: The Arabs made significant advances in mathematics, developing algebra—which was unknown to the Greeks—and introducing Arabic numerals, which made calculations much more convenient than using the Roman system.

Query_Text_cn: 但是，也许是由干受了斯开赫茨德的童话故事的影响，他们在天文学和化学方面的工作几乎都是局限于追求一些荒诞的目的，例如根据一个人出生时星座的位置来预言他的一生（占星学）以及寻找把普通物质变为贵重黄金的方法（炼金术）等。
Translation: However, perhaps influenced by the fairy tales of Scheherazade, their work in astronomy and chemistry was almost entirely limited to the pursuit of some absurd goals, such as predicting a person's entire life based on the position of the stars at their birth (astrology), and seeking methods to turn ordinary substances into precious gold (alchemy).

Query_Text_cn: 他们在物理学方面似乎没有做什么工作，但是，炼金术当然也可以看成是把一种化学元素变为另一种化学元素的現代技术的先驱。
Translation: They do not seem to have done much work in the field of physics; however, alchemy can certainly be regarded as the precursor to modern technology that transforms one chemical element into another.

Query_Text_cn: 然而，“当摩尔人完成了他的使命时，摩尔人就一定走了”，十二世纪时，由于成吉思汗的人侵和基督教十字军对圣地（巴勒斯坦）的持续征讨，阿拉伯王国很快就被征服了。
Translation: However, "when the Moor has fulfilled his mission, the Moor must leave." In the twelfth century, due to the invasions of Genghis Khan and the continuous crusades by Christians against the Holy Land (Palestine), the Arab kingdoms were soon conquered.

Query_Text_cn: 这时候，欧洲国家正在慢慢从中世纪的浑沌状态中苏醒过来，学术研究又开始发展起来了。
Translation: At this time, European countries were gradually awakening from the chaotic state of the Middle Ages, and academic research began to flourish once again.

Query_Text_cn: 公元784年，法兰克帝国的统治者查理曼大帝命令他的广大领土上所有的教堂都必须附设学校，公元1100年，巴黎大学建立了。
Translation: In 784 AD, Charlemagne, the ruler of the Frankish Empire, ordered that all churches throughout his vast territories must establish schools. In 1100 AD, the University of Paris was founded.

Query_Text_cn: 不久以后，又建立了波洛尼亚大学、牛津大学和剑桥大学，它们很快成为公认的学术活动屮心。
Translation: Soon after, the universities of Bologna, Oxford, and Cambridge were established, and they quickly became recognized centers of academic activity.

Query_Text_cn: 常规的学习课程计有“三学科”和“四学科”，前者包括拉丁语法、修辞和逻辑，后者包括算术、几何、音乐与天文。
Translation: The standard curriculum consisted of the "trivium" and the "quadrivium," with the former including Latin grammar, rhetoric, and logic, and the latter comprising arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy.

Query_Text_cn: 但是，教育仍然处在教会的严格监督之下，各基督教国家的大学必须得到罗马教皇的批准才得以继续存在。
Translation: However, education remained under the strict supervision of the Church, and universities in all Christian countries could continue to exist only with the approval of the Pope in Rome.

Query_Text_cn: 学习主要是依据亚里斯多德的著作，那是由阿拉伯人翻译后传入欧洲的。
Translation: Learning was primarily based on the works of Aristotle, which were introduced to Europe after being translated by the Arabs.

Query_Text_cn: 前面说过，亚里斯多德虽然在其它许多方面有着辉煌的成就，但在物理学领域里就相形见绌了，肯定不会有助于刚刚从千年沉睡中苏醒过来的欧洲物理学的复兴的。
Translation: As previously mentioned, although Aristotle achieved remarkable success in many other fields, he was comparatively lacking in the realm of physics and certainly would not have contributed to the revival of European physics, which had just awakened from a thousand-year slumber.

Query_Text_cn: 在知识传播的种种重要因素中，有一个因素是十五世纪中叶在德国的梅恩兹一个名叫福斯特的人的工场中发明了印刷机。这些早期的印刷品中，最重要的一本书无疑是哥白尼所著的《天体运行论》了（公元1543年在纽伦堡出版）他书中确立立了以太阳为中心的新的世界体系。
Translation: Among the many important factors in the dissemination of knowledge, one was the invention of the printing press in the mid-fifteenth century at the workshop of a man named Fust in Mainz, Germany. Among these early printed works, the most significant was undoubtedly Copernicus's "On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres," published in Nuremberg in 1543, in which he established a new heliocentric model of the universe.

Query_Text_cn: 但是为了避免被教会放逐，书中不得不加了一个前言（也许是由出版者奥仙德自己写的，没有让哥白尼知道），前言里说，书中所表达的全部思想只有纯粹臆测的性质，无非是一种数学练习，而不是对真实物体的描写。
Translation: However, in order to avoid excommunication by the Church, a preface had to be added to the book (perhaps written by the publisher Osiander himself, without Copernicus's knowledge), stating that all the ideas expressed in the book were purely speculative in nature, merely a mathematical exercise rather than a depiction of real objects.

Query_Text_cn: 在这一时期中，占星学与真正科学的混杂也许可以从开普勒所著《神密的宇宙》一书中引述的下面一段话得到最好的说明，开普勒是行星运动的基本定律的发现者。
Translation: During this period, the intermingling of astrology and true science is perhaps best illustrated by the following passage quoted from Kepler's work *The Mysterium Cosmographicum*; Kepler was the discoverer of the fundamental laws of planetary motion.

Query_Text_cn: 七个月前我曾答应写一本书，据学者们判断，它是一本精彩而给人印象深刻的书，远比一切年历之类的东西要好，现在我向你们——仁慈的朋友、高贵的先生们献上这本书，虽然它涉及的范围狭窄，但却是我自己真诚努力的成果,而且讨论的是一个奇妙的课题。
Translation: Seven months ago, I promised to write a book which, according to scholars, is considered to be both brilliant and impressive—far superior to any almanac or similar publication. Now, I present this book to you, my kind friends and distinguished gentlemen. Although its scope is limited, it is the result of my sincere efforts and discusses a fascinating subject.

Query_Text_cn: 假如你们追求新奇，这个课题却是由我第一次向全人类提出的。
Translation: If you seek novelty, this topic is one that I am presenting to all of humanity for the very first time.

Query_Text_cn: 假如你们迫求尊严，没有什么东西比上帝的宏伟壮丽的殿堂更髙贵、更美丽了。
Translation: If you seek dignity, nothing is nobler or more beautiful than the magnificent and majestic temple of God.

Query_Text_cn: 要是你们希望知道秘密，自然界中从来没有什么比它更奥妙的了。
Translation: If you wish to know the secret, there is nothing in nature more mysterious than it.

Query_Text_cn: 尽管如此，我的目的不会使每个人都满意，因为它的用处对不爱思考的人来说并不明显。
