You will encounter many experiences you have never faced before, such as searching for accommodation, managing your own finances, embarking on a new social life, forming new friendships, and developing both physically and mentally. These matters are varied and numerous, but among them, those related to the development of your intellect deserve your utmost attention.

Query_Text_cn: 老实说，现在你真要自动地使用你自己的心力了，不能像从前一样咧。所以最好在尚未投入战争之前先把几个关于这件事情的问题来考察一下。
Translation: To be honest, you now truly need to actively engage your own mental faculties; you can no longer rely on the ways of the past. Therefore, it is best to examine several questions related to this matter before becoming involved in the conflict.

Query_Text_cn: 听讲和笔记你将要遇到的第一种困难或许就是听讲了。
Translation: The first difficulty you may encounter is likely to be listening to lectures.

Query_Text_cn: 听讲是没有什么课本的，所以是你以前所未曾经惯的事情。
Translation: There are no textbooks for listening to lectures, so it is something you have not been accustomed to before.

Query_Text_cn: 讲演者所讲的说话，一经出了他的口，便不能再行听到了。
Translation: Once the speaker's words have left his mouth, they can no longer be heard again.

Query_Text_cn: 而且不能像读书一样，偶有忽略尚可重新读过的。
Translation: Moreover, unlike reading a book, where occasional omissions can be remedied by rereading, this is not possible here.

Query_Text_cn: 不但如此你还要养成一种新的记忆力以记忆听到的讲词。
Translation: Moreover, you must also develop a new kind of memory to retain the words you hear in speeches.

Query_Text_cn: 为帮助这种记忆并使听到的材料成为系统起见，你又要发展出一种做笔记底材能来。
Translation: To facilitate this kind of memory and to systematically organize the material you hear, you need to develop a method for taking notes.

Query_Text_cn: 然而却是大学生活上的一个极重要的方面，所以也要着实研究一下。
Translation: However, it is an extremely important aspect of university life and therefore deserves thorough study.

Query_Text_cn: （二）读物底数量大学生活底又一种特点，便是应读的书籍底数量之多。
Translation: Another characteristic of university life is the sheer volume of required reading materials.

Query_Text_cn: 从前每个课目只消一本课本的，现在要用好几本了。
Translation: In the past, each subject required only one textbook, but now several are needed.

Query_Text_cn: 从前那种从容暇豫的读法和轻便容易的功课，现在都不能有了。
Translation: The leisurely and unhurried way of reading, as well as the light and easy assignments of the past, are no longer possible now.

Query_Text_cn: 现在你恐怕天天要读五十页或一百页的艰难读物了。
Translation: Now you probably have to read fifty or even a hundred pages of challenging material every day.

Query_Text_cn: 所以你非读得快并理解得快不可。
Translation: Therefore, you must read quickly and comprehend quickly.

Query_Text_cn: 确实说，经济两字便是你的座右金箴了。
Translation: Indeed, "economy" is truly your guiding principle.

Query_Text_cn: （三）学业底质量不但学业底数量要加多，同时学业底质量也要增高因为现在你既然做了大学生，社会上已把你当一个很有学问的人看待，因而对你的希望也较前更大了。
Translation: (3) Not only should the quantity of academic foundation be increased, but its quality must also be improved. Now that you are a university student, society regards you as a highly knowledgeable individual and therefore has greater expectations of you than before.

Query_Text_cn: 再用学校里的话来讲，则倘使你要在大学中得到一个九十五分，那么你在功课上该费的心力必定要比你在中学里想得到同样的分数时所费的心力更加来得多才行。因为在大学里，不但你的功课较从前更觉艰深，而且要争个首位时也较从前格外吃力了。
Translation: To put it in terms used in schools, if you want to earn a score of ninety-five in university, you must devote much more effort to your studies than you would have needed to achieve the same score in high school. This is because not only are your courses more challenging in university, but competing for the top spot is also significantly more demanding than before.

Query_Text_cn: 原来在中学时你或许是一个高材生，如今到了大学，则四面八方底其他高材生也都同你来相会了。
Translation: Back in high school, you might have been a top student, but now in university, outstanding students from all directions have come together with you.

Query_Text_cn: 这就是说，从今以后，你对于学业底质量不得不设法加高了。
Translation: This means that from now on, you will have to find ways to improve the quality of your academic work.

Query_Text_cn: （四）功课表底必要大学生活之再一种难处，使是没有日课表。
Translation: Another difficulty inherent in university life is the absence of a daily class schedule.

Query_Text_cn: 学校所帮你派定的唯一的作业时间，只是那每星期十五个钟头左右的讲堂生活罢了。
Translation: The only designated study time assigned to you by the school is merely the approximately fifteen hours of classroom instruction each week.

Query_Text_cn: 其余的时间便全要靠你自己的处置咧。
Translation: The rest of the time will be entirely up to your own discretion.

Query_Text_cn: 倘使你要用最经济的时间和最经济的劳力来完成你的学业，那么，这功课表底问题实在是一件最足考虑的事情啊。
Translation: If you wish to complete your studies with the most efficient use of time and effort, then the issue of your class schedule is truly something that deserves the utmost consideration.

Query_Text_cn: （五）习惯底养成和自力底必要以上已把几个智力上的难题简单地考察完了。
Translation:
5. The Formation of Habits and the Necessity of Self-Reliance

The above has briefly examined several intellectual challenges.

Query_Text_cn: 在这样的情形之下，如若你要适应大学底环境，非从速养成许多新习惯下手不可。
Translation: Under such circumstances, if you wish to adapt to the university environment, you must promptly develop a number of new habits.

Query_Text_cn: 原来这些困难底最终问题，只是一个习惯之养成底问题。因为大学教育虽有两方面——知识底获得和习惯底养成——然其最重要的方面却在后者。
Translation: It turns out that the fundamental issue behind these difficulties is merely a matter of habit formation. Although university education encompasses two aspects—acquisition of knowledge and cultivation of habits—the latter is, in fact, the most important.

Query_Text_cn: 唯有种种修学的习惯，一经养成了之后，便为终身的财产了。
Translation: Only the various habits of study, once cultivated, become a lifelong asset.

Query_Text_cn: 这些习惯包括着种种方法：如把捉事实底方法，推求事实底方法，集中注意底方法等等。
Translation: These habits include various methods, such as methods for grasping facts, methods for deducing facts, and methods for concentrating attention, among others.

Query_Text_cn: 各种课业都不过是帮你养成这些习惯的手段。
Translation: All kinds of coursework are merely means to help you develop these habits.

Query_Text_cn: 例如学校里所以要你做出许多文章来，为的并不是要你对于世界上的文学有所增益：也不是要你的教师见了欢喜，只因为这件事情可以帮你养成自由地发表思想底习惯之故。
Translation: For example, the reason schools require you to write many essays is not to enhance your knowledge of world literature, nor to please your teachers, but simply because this practice helps you develop the habit of freely expressing your thoughts.

Query_Text_cn: 又如：你是将要常常被邀入科学试验室里去做种种实验工夫的，这也不是想要你去发明一些尚未发明的事物，只不过要你得到一些研究科学底习惯和独自寻求知识底习惯罢了。
Translation: For example, you will often be invited into scientific laboratories to conduct various experiments. This is not intended for you to invent something that has not yet been discovered, but rather to help you develop habits of scientific inquiry and independent pursuit of knowledge.

Query_Text_cn: 虽然，课程和教师，在教育过程上，终不过是手段罢了，原动力还在你自己身上呢。
Translation: Although courses and teachers are merely tools in the educational process, the true driving force lies within yourself.

Query_Text_cn: 假使没有你自己方面的努力，那么无论课程如何完美，教师如何有名，你的教育到底也是好不来的。
Translation: Without your own efforts, no matter how perfect the curriculum or how renowned the teachers are, your education will ultimately not be successful.

Query_Text_cn: 切不要把你自己当作一只空桶看侍，以为知识只要装了进去就是了。
Translation: Never regard yourself as an empty vessel, thinking that knowledge is simply something to be filled in.

Query_Text_cn: 须知道要得到一种教育，非先建设一种自动的——不是被动的——态度不可。
Translation: It must be understood that to receive an education, one must first cultivate an automatic—not passive—attitude.

Query_Text_cn: 求学问是一种自动的努力，不是一种被动的吸收底进程，越是你的活动竭力，则你的能力将越是伟大。
Translation: The pursuit of knowledge is an active endeavor, not a passive process of absorption. The more diligently you apply yourself, the greater your abilities will become.

Query_Text_cn: （六）良好法式底重要要体育之发达，第一要使一切事情都在良好的法式中做去。
Translation: A sound legal framework is essential for the development of sports; above all, it is necessary to ensure that everything is conducted within a proper legal order.

Query_Text_cn: 要智育之发达，也是这样。
Translation: The development of intellectual education follows the same principle.

Query_Text_cn: 最有出息的人，便是那能够用最少的劳力和最短的时间以完成一定事物的人。
Translation: The most accomplished individuals are those who can complete a given task with the least effort and in the shortest amount of time.

Query_Text_cn: 所以你总应该时时留心去避掉一切无用的和有碍的方法，尽力去图谋修学上的良好法式之发展。
Translation: Therefore, you should always be vigilant in avoiding all useless and obstructive methods, and strive to promote the development of effective approaches in your studies.

Query_Text_cn: 在发端之初，这事尤为必要如是则智力上的基础方始可立，然后再处处用精锐的眼光去留心，务使建筑在这基础上的材料和工程件件都可以当得起“精悍的结构”这个名称。
Translation: At the outset, this is particularly necessary, for only then can an intellectual foundation be established. Subsequently, one must observe everything with keen insight to ensure that every material and component built upon this foundation truly deserves the name of a "robust structure."

Query_Text_cn: 大多数受教育的人们有时候都要做点笔记。
Translation: Most educated people need to take notes from time to time.

Query_Text_cn: 大学生尤其要做；然而因为做来不得法，所以往往没有成效。
Translation: College students, in particular, should do this; however, due to improper methods, their efforts often yield little result.

Query_Text_cn: 假使细心研究一下，就可知道做笔记也有一定的规则或原理。
Translation: If you study carefully, you will find that there are certain rules or principles to note-taking.

Query_Text_cn: 如其照规则照原理做去，就可增加不少修学能力。
Translation: If one follows the rules and principles, one can greatly enhance their learning ability.

Query_Text_cn: 笔记底用处做笔记第一要问笔记底用处。
Translation: The primary purpose of taking notes is to first ask about the use of the notes.

Query_Text_cn: 这个明白了，便有标准在手，可以免除许多误谬。
Translation: Once this is understood and a standard is established, many errors and misunderstandings can be avoided.

Query_Text_cn: 笔记底用处有三：一是整理每天底课业；一是提要钩玄以备临时的急读；一是为永久的职业上的应用。
Translation: There are three main purposes for taking notes: first, to organize daily coursework; second, to summarize key points for quick reference when needed; and third, to serve as a resource for long-term professional use.

Query_Text_cn: 一本笔记簿可说是一件最贵重的物品。
Translation: A notebook can be considered one of the most valuable possessions.

Query_Text_cn: 在学生时代所做的笔记，到将来的职业生活上也许尚有价值的。
Translation: The notes taken during one's student days may still hold value in future professional life.

Query_Text_cn: 知道了这个道理，才好去做笔记，并且常常可以因之决定如何做法了。
Translation: Once you understand this principle, you can take notes more effectively and often determine how to proceed accordingly.

Query_Text_cn: 大学生活上需要笔记之处大概有三：听讲时阅书时，在试验室里作工时。
Translation: There are generally three occasions in university life where taking notes is necessary: during lectures, while reading books, and when working in the laboratory.

Query_Text_cn: 故我们就照这三项来考虑笔记法底问题。
Translation: Therefore, we will address the issue of note-taking methods based on these three aspects.

Query_Text_cn: （二）讲演笔记关于听讲时的笔记一事，有两种极端的主张：一种主张全部记录，一种主张完全不记。
Translation:
(2) Lecture Notes

Regarding the practice of taking notes during lectures, there are two extreme viewpoints: one advocates recording everything, while the other advocates not taking any notes at all.

Query_Text_cn: 两种主张都可产生不良的结果。自然照第一种见解说，完全的记录是很有意思的。
Translation: Both arguments can lead to undesirable outcomes. Naturally, according to the first view, a complete record is very interesting.

Query_Text_cn: 不过主张第二种见解的人也可说明废去笔记非但无害而且有益底理由：第一，做笔记要耗费许多许多的时间；第二讲词中有许多材料是不值永久保存的，听讲的人只要能够将要点扼住就够了。
Translation: However, proponents of the second view can also explain that abolishing note-taking is not only harmless but even beneficial for the following reasons: First, taking notes consumes a great deal of time; second, much of the material in lectures is not worth preserving permanently, and it is sufficient for listeners to grasp only the main points.

Query_Text_cn: 至于讲演人为增加其见解底势力起见，因而附入的其他种种说话并无本身上的重要，我们正可不必多所顾及。
Translation: As for the various remarks added by the speaker to enhance the force of their opinions, since they are not inherently important, we need not pay much attention to them.

Query_Text_cn: 此外，还有一种更加有力的反对理由：倘使你在听讲时只把注意力用在逐字逐句底纪录上面，毫无工夫去“思想，”那么，你就无异变成了一部自动的誊写机。
Translation: Moreover, there is an even stronger objection: if, during a lecture, you focus solely on recording every word and sentence without having any time to "think," then you are no different from an automatic transcription machine.

Query_Text_cn: 了一班有经验的速记家说，他们因为做机械的记录做惯了，以致对于所听见的话竟是茫然不知其什么意思。
Translation: Some experienced stenographers have said that, because they are so accustomed to mechanically recording what they hear, they are often completely unaware of the actual meaning of the words.

Query_Text_cn: 你是学生，更不该这样去出神，免致对于所讲底意思全然不晓。
Translation: You are a student, so you should be even less likely to let your mind wander, lest you completely miss the meaning of what is being taught.

Query_Text_cn: 虽然，一般学生之所以定要从事于所谓全部记录者，也有缘故，就因为他们不敢信托自家的记忆力。
Translation: Although ordinary students insist on acting as so-called comprehensive recorders, there is a reason for this: they do not dare to trust their own memory.

Query_Text_cn: 然而这也实是不必多虑的事情。只要听讲时能够施以精密的注意，并作成有理性的联想，那就无事不能记着了。
Translation: However, this is not something to be overly concerned about. As long as one pays close attention during the lecture and forms rational associations, there will be nothing that cannot be remembered.

Query_Text_cn: 所以你对于一种讲演，务必自由使用你自己的思想去和讲演者作腹辩，质问他的议论，把你自己的经验和读书底结果提出来同他的说话比较着。
Translation: Therefore, when listening to a speech, you must freely use your own thoughts to internally debate with the speaker, question their arguments, and bring forth your own experiences and the results of your reading to compare with what they are saying.

Query_Text_cn: 要而言之，你必需抱取一种思想自动底态度。无论什么东西凡是妨害这个态度并要使你成为被动的，都该避掉他。
Translation: In short, you must adopt an attitude of intellectual initiative. Anything that hinders this attitude and seeks to make you passive should be avoided.

Query_Text_cn: （三）读书笔记讲演笔记上所有的全部纪录和完全不记底问题，在读书笔记上也要发生出来。
Translation: (3) All records and issues of complete omission in both reading notes and lecture notes must also be reflected in the reading notes.

Query_Text_cn: 虽然，笔记是终竟少不来的，只不要太长太笨罢了。大约说你的读书笔记应该是一种缩记，是将着书人的议论用你自己的文字省略地写出来的一种缩记，不要像个抄本一般。
Translation: Although taking notes is ultimately indispensable, they should not be too lengthy or cumbersome. Generally speaking, your reading notes should be a form of abridged summary, condensing the author's arguments into your own words, rather than resembling a mere transcription.

Query_Text_cn: 往住有些学生好把原书底文句读到一句写下一句，停一会如再读到一句则再写下一句，以为这样直抄下来便是万全的办法了。
Translation: Some students tend to read a sentence from the original text and write it down, then pause, and when they read another sentence, they write it down again, believing that copying directly in this manner is the safest approach.

Query_Text_cn: 其实这是一种大坏的习惯，原书所有思想底脉络都被破碎完了。况且各种称单独的句子又往往没甚意思，不能代表著者的真实思想。
Translation: In fact, this is a very bad habit, as it completely fragments the underlying logic of the original work. Moreover, individual sentences taken out of context often carry little meaning and cannot represent the author's true ideas.

Query_Text_cn: 所以较好的法子是：先把一大段或一小段底全文从头至尾阅读一下，然后把原书放置一边，再用你自己的文字将所读的写出来，回来再把所写的同原文对校一番，看有没有捉着焦点。
Translation: Therefore, a better approach is to first read through a large or small section of the entire text from beginning to end, then set the original book aside and use your own words to write out what you have read. Afterwards, compare what you have written with the original text to see if you have grasped the main points.

Query_Text_cn: 三则使你对于原文能够见得其思想，不是仅仅作文字上的阅读；结果，由这种方法所处理过的材料，比之用支离破碎的方法所处理的，更容易记忆得长久。
Translation: These three points enable you to grasp the underlying ideas of the original text, rather than merely reading the words. As a result, material processed using this method is easier to remember for a longer period compared to material handled in a fragmented manner.

Query_Text_cn: 简言之，这样的一种读书法不但可以造就良好的记忆，并且可以养成智力上的一切良好习惯。
Translation: In short, this method of reading not only fosters good memory but also cultivates all beneficial intellectual habits.

Query_Text_cn: 无论读什么东西，总不要忘却你是一个能思想的人，不是一块海绵。
Translation: No matter what you read, never forget that you are a thinking person, not a sponge.

Query_Text_cn: 要记着你是不要将所读的东西通统无条件地吸收起来的，却是要估计和思索的。
Translation: You must remember not to unconditionally absorb everything you read, but rather to evaluate and reflect on it.

Query_Text_cn: 大概做书人所要说的话都可以在标题中看出，你在读时可先把这个记了，然后再去寻他的答案。
Translation: What the author intends to convey is often reflected in the title; you may first take note of this as you read, and then look for the answers within the text.

Query_Text_cn: 及至重要的部分既然看好，就把原书翻转，提出个纲领来，看看著者是否供给了你所需要的材料。
Translation: Once you have identified the key sections, turn the original book around and formulate an outline to see whether the author has provided the materials you need.

Query_Text_cn: 这样，读书才有指导，思想也有定向了。
Translation: In this way, reading becomes guided and our thinking gains direction.

Query_Text_cn: 以上讲读书笔记已牵及“怎样读法”底问题了。这个问题是大可研究的，所以我们索性再费点时间来讨论一下罢。
Translation: The above reading notes have already touched upon the question of "how to read." This is a topic worthy of in-depth study, so let us take some more time to discuss it further.

Query_Text_cn: 每读一书，当有几许发端的礼节。
Translation: Each time you begin reading a book, there should be a certain sense of ceremony at the outset.

Query_Text_cn: 这并不是说，读一本书该有什么形质上的举动，却是指心思上的行径而言。
Translation: This does not refer to any specific physical actions one should take when reading a book, but rather to the attitude and approach of the mind.

Query_Text_cn: 观察书名，认清楚怎样的范围是该书所想包括的。
Translation: Observe the title of the book to clearly understand the scope it intends to cover.

Query_Text_cn: 观察著者的姓名。
Translation: Observe the author's name.

Query_Text_cn: 倘使这书是你要常常用着的，那么再设法去查考著者在该项学问上有怎样的地位。
Translation: If this is a book you will be using frequently, then you should make an effort to investigate the author's standing in the relevant field.

Query_Text_cn: 在每书底题页上，在姓氏录上，或传记辞典上，都可得到这种消息。
Translation: Such information can be found on the title page at the bottom of each book, in the register of surnames, or in biographical dictionaries.

Query_Text_cn: 将书中的序文略看一遍，在或种情形之下，这序文又该仔细阅览。
Translation: First, skim through the preface of the book; under certain circumstances, the preface should then be read carefully.

Query_Text_cn: 至其出版年代也须注意，因为如此，则对于书中材料之新旧，也可得到一点观念了。
Translation: Attention must also be paid to the publication date, as this will provide some insight into the currency of the materials contained in the book.

Query_Text_cn: 将书中的目录略看一过。
Translation: I briefly glanced through the table of contents in the book.

Query_Text_cn: 倘然你对于这书所述及的事情早已熟习过了，而这目录却又是一个仔细的大纲，则你就不必阅览全书，只消将这个目录看了就够。
Translation: If you are already familiar with the matters discussed in this book, and this table of contents serves as a detailed outline, then there is no need to read the entire book; simply reviewing the table of contents will suffice.

Query_Text_cn: 或则如果你是要把该书摘读几处的，别对于这个目录也要看一遍，以便明白你所摘读的部分和全书底关系。
Translation: Or, if you intend to excerpt a few passages from the book, you should also review the table of contents to understand how the sections you select relate to the entire work.

Query_Text_cn: 对于书中所附的索引要作合法的使用，这是可以替你省却许多时间的。
Translation: Making proper use of the index provided in the book can save you a great deal of time.

Query_Text_cn: （四）试验室里的笔记这一类的笔记底法式往往随科学底性质而异，且往往由教授所指定。
Translation: (4) The format for laboratory notes often varies according to the nature of the science involved and is usually specified by the professor.

Query_Text_cn: 大概可照下面的次序书写：先标明目的，次记所用的仪器，次方法，次结果，次结论。
Translation: The following sequence can generally be followed when writing: first state the purpose, then list the instruments used, followed by the methods, then the results, and finally the conclusion.

Query_Text_cn: 如果教师预先另有详细的吩咐，则你就可以仔细听从他。
Translation: If the teacher has given specific instructions in advance, you may follow them carefully.

Query_Text_cn: 对于整洁两字务必特别留心。
Translation: Be particularly attentive to the concept of cleanliness.

Query_Text_cn: 教师常常说，试验笔记簿之最大缺点便是不能整洁。
Translation: Teachers often say that the greatest drawback of laboratory notebooks is that they cannot be kept neat.

Query_Text_cn: 须知道“不能整洁”四个字就最容易惹起恶果。当教师修正这种笔记时，他往往感到不少的困难，结果是使他顾不得自己的意志，也顾不得他的学生，竟是怀着一种偏见了。
Translation: It must be understood that the words "cannot be neat" are most likely to lead to negative consequences. When teachers try to correct such notes, they often encounter considerable difficulties. As a result, they may disregard their own intentions as well as those of their students, and end up harboring a certain bias.

Query_Text_cn: 如果你的笔记做得整洁了，那么你在科学实验底课程上占优势的机会，就可因此加多这是一定好说的。
Translation: If your notes are kept neat and organized, your chances of gaining an advantage in science laboratory courses will certainly increase.

Query_Text_cn: （五）笔记之形式上的事项笔记簿底内容方面已算讨论完结，但是他的形式方面也有同样的重要。二十世纪之主要关键是“经济”两字。凡百事业都趋向于免除耗费一方面走。
Translation:
(v) Formal Aspects of Note-taking

The content of the notebook has been thoroughly discussed, but its formal aspects are equally important. The main keyword of the twentieth century is "economy." All undertakings are moving toward eliminating waste in every aspect.

Query_Text_cn: 故笔记之形式上的事项也要以能够节省我们的时间和心力为最要。
Translation: Therefore, the format of our notes should primarily aim to save our time and effort.

Query_Text_cn: 记当用墨水书写。
Translation: Records should be written in ink.

Query_Text_cn: 铅笔写的，数月以后，便要模糊不清，难以认读了。
Translation: Written in pencil, it will become blurred and difficult to read after a few months.

Query_Text_cn: 须记着一本笔记簿是从今以后尚要应用十廿年的，所以要写得能够耐久为要。
Translation: It must be remembered that a notebook is something that will be used for the next ten or twenty years, so it should be written in a way that ensures its durability.

Query_Text_cn: 要写得清楚这是无须多说的了。
Translation: It goes without saying that clarity is essential.

Query_Text_cn: 因为常识就告诉我们说，字迹模糊的书写物，过了些时连写者自己都看不出来的。
Translation: Because common sense tells us that handwriting which is blurred will become illegible even to the writer themselves after some time.

Query_Text_cn: 造句时也要留心，不要使你的笔记仅由几许零零碎碎的不相联络的字眼组成起来。
Translation: When constructing sentences, be mindful not to let your notes consist merely of a few scattered, disconnected words.

Query_Text_cn: 果然，在逼迫之下，很难造成完全的文句，只有先行这里记下一个字，那里记下一个字，然后靠着那半真不切的记忆，希望事后有工夫时再去补充完篇，但是稍有经验的人便能立刻证明这种希望是不能实现的，所以还是早些努力去用有意义的短句写成，并使各部分的网目互相衔接为妙。
Translation: As expected, under pressure, it is difficult to produce complete sentences. One can only jot down a word here and a word there, relying on a half-true and unreliable memory, hoping to fill in the rest when there is time later. However, anyone with a bit of experience can immediately attest that such hopes are unlikely to be realized. Therefore, it is better to make an effort early on to write meaningful short sentences and ensure that the various parts are interconnected.

Query_Text_cn: 第四个问题，是关于笔纪簿底大小和形式的。
Translation: The fourth question concerns the size and format of the notebook.

Query_Text_cn: 这个问题底解决，一半要看课程底性质，一半要照个人的喜好而定。
Translation: The resolution of this issue depends partly on the nature of the course and partly on individual preferences.

Query_Text_cn: 大概使各科底笔记并成一本，较为便利有用。
Translation: It is more convenient and useful to combine the notes from all subjects into a single volume.

Query_Text_cn: 许多人常常欢喜用小本的笔记簿，以衣袋中可以携带为度；因为如此别偶有余暇的时候，便可以取出来阅览的。
Translation: Many people often prefer to use small notebooks that can be carried in their pockets, so that whenever they have a moment of leisure, they can take them out and read.

Query_Text_cn: 大概说来后者较前者为可取。
Translation: Generally speaking, the latter is preferable to the former.

Query_Text_cn: 因为散叶是容易添入的，而且一个学程讲完之后，各篇章也容易按照次序并成一起。
Translation: Because loose leaves are easy to add, and after completing a course of study, the various chapters can also be easily compiled together in order.

Query_Text_cn: （六）余论我们已经知道笔记做得好，就有种种利益。例如时间上的经济温习时之便利，记忆底保留等等，都是显而易见的。
Translation:
(6) Conclusion

We already know that taking good notes brings various benefits. For example, it saves time, makes reviewing more convenient, and helps retain information in memory—all of which are obvious advantages.

Query_Text_cn: 但是其中还有他种好处，虽非易见，却是更为重要。
Translation: However, there are other benefits that, though not immediately apparent, are even more important.

Query_Text_cn: 因为从此你的脑子里便生了种种稀不易消灭的效果了。
Translation: From then on, various effects that are difficult to eliminate will arise in your mind.

Query_Text_cn: 正确的思想之习惯，便是良好的笔记底第一效果。
Translation: The habit of correct thinking is the primary benefit of good note-taking.

Query_Text_cn: 如果你在这材干——笔记——上发展得好了，那么，其他的材干，如观念之了解和融化，知识之保存和产出，以及理性底独立相贯彻等，也都有相应的进步了。
Translation: If you make good progress in this skill—note-taking—then other skills, such as understanding and assimilating concepts, preserving and producing knowledge, and consistently maintaining independent reasoning, will also improve accordingly.

Query_Text_cn: 当修学时，我们的脑筋就起一种活动。这虽是大多数的人所多少有点知道的事情，但是要对于这种活动底性质有种确切的知识，却是不大有的。
Translation: When we study, our minds become active. Although most people are somewhat aware of this, few possess a precise understanding of the nature of this mental activity.

Query_Text_cn: 然而知道了这种活动底性质，别在思想过程之了解上又是大有帮助的，所以我们将简短地把这种活动底机关即脑髓并其他相关的东西来考察一下。
Translation: However, understanding the fundamental nature of this activity is also greatly beneficial to our comprehension of the thought process. Therefore, we will briefly examine the organ responsible for this activity—the brain—and other related elements.

Query_Text_cn: 肉眼中所见的脑髓之构造照肉眼看来，脑髓是一种胶状的物质，在头盖骨当中，有一层厚膜包覆着。
Translation: To the naked eye, the structure of the brain appears as a gelatinous substance enclosed within the skull and covered by a thick membrane.

Query_Text_cn: 脑之底部，有一条由神经纤维组成的长索，向脊骨一直下去，这就叫做脊髓。
Translation: At the base of the brain, there is a long cord composed of nerve fibers that extends down along the spine; this is called the spinal cord.

Query_Text_cn: 脊髄之大部分约有一小指之粗，惟下部则渐细。
Translation: The majority of the spinal cord is approximately the thickness of a little finger, but it gradually tapers toward the lower end.

Query_Text_cn: 从脊髓全部底两边，发出三十一对神经来，布满全身脑髓脊髓并其全部的神经，就叫做神经系统。
Translation: From both sides of the entire lower part of the spinal cord, thirty-one pairs of nerves emerge and spread throughout the body. The brain, spinal cord, and all their associated nerves together are referred to as the nervous system.

Query_Text_cn: 由此可见，我们虽说思想和脑髓有密切的关系，但还该扩大一些说思想是和全部神经系统有关系的了。
Translation: It is evident that, although thought is closely related to the brain, it should be further stated that thought is connected to the entire nervous system.

Query_Text_cn: 从显微镜中所见的构造神经系统，照肉眼看来，虽明明为无数相异的物质所组成，但是倘用显微镜来观察，则就可知道其各部分在构造上是一概相同的。
Translation: The structure of the nervous system observed under a microscope, although clearly composed of countless distinct substances to the naked eye, reveals under microscopic examination that all its parts are structurally identical.

Query_Text_cn: 神经系统之构造上的单位就叫做神经细胞。
Translation: The structural unit of the nervous system is called the nerve cell.

Query_Text_cn: 每个神经细胞都由许多突起及一个细胞体所组成。突起是从细胞体的两头分射出来的。
Translation: Each nerve cell consists of numerous processes and a cell body. The processes extend from both ends of the cell body.

Query_Text_cn: 这种细胞长的约有三英尺，短的不过当一英寸中的一个分数。
Translation: These cells can be as long as about three feet, while the shortest are only a fraction of an inch.

Query_Text_cn: 由几百万这样的细胞，参互错综地组合着，并布满于全身，便成了个神经系统。
Translation: Millions of such cells, intricately interconnected and distributed throughout the body, together form the nervous system.

Query_Text_cn: 讲到精神作用（如思想，感觉，意志等，）和神经系统究竟怎样发生关系，我们尚未确切知道。
Translation: We do not yet know exactly how mental functions, such as thought, feeling, and will, relate to the nervous system.

Query_Text_cn: 不过每逢我们心中起了事端时，我们的神经系统上也有变化发生，这是我们所的确晓得的。
Translation: However, whenever turmoil arises in our hearts, changes also occur in our nervous system, which we know for certain.

Query_Text_cn: 所以在修学上讲，每逢你在记忆一种外国字，或思索一个几何学上的题目时，你的神经系统上也正在发生变化。
Translation: Therefore, in terms of learning, whenever you memorize a foreign word or ponder a problem in geometry, changes are also taking place in your nervous system.

Query_Text_cn: 因此现在的问题只是：这些变化底本质究竟是怎么样的。
Translation: Therefore, the question now is simply: what is the true nature of these changes?

Query_Text_cn: 照目前的知识，神经系统底运动大概可说是一种发生于神经细胞间的化学上的变化。
Translation: According to current knowledge, neural activity can generally be described as a chemical change occurring between nerve cells.

Query_Text_cn: 这种变化，我们称之为神经流。
Translation: We refer to this change as neural flow.

Query_Text_cn: 神经流沿着神经细胞流去，速度很大，一秒钟可以流一百多呎。神经流之发生不在一个单独的神经细胞上，必对许多细胞通力合作。神经流就从甲细胞通过乙细胞，再通过丙细胞等等。
Translation: The nerve impulse travels along the nerve cells at a high speed, covering more than a hundred feet per second. The generation of a nerve impulse does not occur within a single nerve cell; it requires the coordinated effort of many cells. The nerve impulse passes from cell A to cell B, then to cell C, and so on.

Query_Text_cn: 至于神经系统中所起的变化，也不在一个单独的细胞之中，而在各细胞互相结合的部分。
Translation: As for the changes occurring within the nervous system, they do not take place within a single cell, but rather in the interconnected parts among various cells.

Query_Text_cn: 这结合的部分就叫做接触部。关于接触部底真实情形我们虽不能知道，但正可以把这接触部当一扇活斗看待。神经流由甲细胞到乙细胞时必须经过此门。
Translation: This combined part is called the contact area. Although we cannot know the true nature of the contact area, we can regard it as a gate. When the neural flow passes from cell A to cell B, it must go through this gate.

Query_Text_cn: 人生之初，大多数的活门是关闭着的，只有一部分（例如关乎营养作用的）开着。
Translation: At the beginning of life, most of the gateways are closed, with only a few—such as those related to nutrition—remaining open.

Query_Text_cn: 及至受了环境之影响，然后这些活门才松了，使神经之流得由此通过。
Translation: Only after being influenced by the environment do these valves loosen, allowing the flow of nerves to pass through.

Query_Text_cn: 如果我们对于这些活门使用愈力，则我们底启闭也格外容易了。所以所谓学习就不过是一种进行，要神经流通过各细胞时渐渐更觉容易罢了。
Translation: If we exert more force on these valves, opening and closing them becomes much easier for us. Therefore, what we call learning is merely a process, whereby the flow of nerves through various cells gradually becomes easier.

Query_Text_cn: （三）神经细胞之特性如果我们再将神经细胞底特性来考察一下，则我们对于神经系统底活动原理将更为明白。
Translation: (3) Examining the characteristics of nerve cells further will provide us with a clearer understanding of the principles underlying the activities of the nervous system.

Query_Text_cn: 神经细胞之第一种特性是善于接收外来的感触。
Translation: The first characteristic of nerve cells is their ability to efficiently receive external stimuli.

Query_Text_cn: 例如牙医生将你牙肉上的某种神经触着了，则你的痛楚的感觉就要厉害到了不得咧。
Translation: For example, if a dentist touches a certain nerve in your gums, the pain you feel will be extremely intense.

Query_Text_cn: 这种善于感触之特性在教育上是很重要的。假使没有这个，我们就没能力得到知识，甚至要连危险都不知道祸患都不知避了。
Translation: This sensitivity is very important in education. Without it, we would be unable to acquire knowledge, and we might not even recognize danger or know how to avoid disasters.

Query_Text_cn: 神经细胞之第二种特性在修学上有重要意义的，是传导性。
Translation: The second characteristic of nerve cells that holds significant importance in academic study is their conductivity.

Query_Text_cn: 每当一个神经细胞在一端受了刺激时，他就立刻把这刺激从神经流上传给第二个神经细胞，或旁边的其他神经细胞了，好比电流之由甲线传到乙线，再由乙线传到丙线一般。
Translation: Whenever a nerve cell is stimulated at one end, it immediately transmits this stimulus along the nerve current to a second nerve cell or to other adjacent nerve cells, much like an electric current passing from wire A to wire B, and then from wire B to wire C.

Query_Text_cn: 神经细胞之第三种特性在修学上有重要意义的，是善变底能力。
Translation: The third characteristic of nerve cells, which holds significant importance in learning, is their remarkable adaptability.

Query_Text_cn: 有许多有活力的组织，在一定程度中，多是善于变化的。
Translation: There are many dynamic organizations, most of which are adept at adapting to change to a certain extent.

Query_Text_cn: 例如人类的面貌使是善于变化的东西。
Translation: For example, human appearance is something that is adept at changing.

Query_Text_cn: 假使一个人常常装做一种恨怒的容颜，长久了，就会变成一定的相貌的。
Translation: If a person frequently puts on an expression of anger and hatred, over time, it will become a fixed aspect of their appearance.

Query_Text_cn: 神经系统上所有这种变化底能力更加来得大，虽是一种单一的感触也足发生极大的变化。
Translation: The capacity for such changes in the nervous system is even greater; even a single sensation can undergo tremendous transformation.

Query_Text_cn: 记忆之所以能够保存，其基础就在这变化性上面。所以我们说在修学上有极重要的意义。
Translation: The reason why memories can be preserved lies precisely in their variability. Therefore, this holds great significance in the process of learning and cultivation.

Query_Text_cn: （四）神经流底通路神经系统底活动，其大略已如上述。现在要考察神经系统底各部分究竟是怎样互相联络起来的。
Translation: (4) The basic activity of the neural pathways in the nervous system has been roughly described above. Now, we need to examine how the various parts of the nervous system are actually interconnected.

Query_Text_cn: 这就是要讲神经流底通路了。讲先感觉上的通路感觉上的通路在感官中安置着——不但在旧说的五种感官中安置着，且也在筋肉，踺，关节并其他身体的内部器官（如心脏和消化器官等等）当中安置着这许多器官当中都有神经细胞。
Translation: This brings us to the discussion of the neural afferent pathways. The sensory pathways are situated within the sensory organs—not only within the traditionally recognized five senses, but also in the muscles, tendons, joints, and other internal organs of the body, such as the heart and digestive organs. All these organs contain nerve cells.

Query_Text_cn: 这些神经细胞底末端在脊髓上相汇合，然后再进入脑髓中去。
Translation: The basal ends of these nerve cells converge on the spinal cord before entering the brain.

Query_Text_cn: 这种细胞叫做感觉性的神经细胞。他们的功能就在传达消息到脑子里去。
Translation: These cells are called sensory neurons. Their function is to transmit messages to the brain.

Query_Text_cn: 所以说到脑髓底职司，大部分就无异是一个接收感触的报告的总机关。
Translation: Therefore, when it comes to the fundamental function of the brain marrow, for the most part, it is essentially the central organ responsible for receiving and reporting sensations.

Query_Text_cn: 至于机关中所有接收报告的人，也是些神经细胞。这些神经细胞各各处于一定的区域。
Translation: As for all the recipients of reports within the organization, they are also nerve cells. Each of these nerve cells is located in a specific area.

Query_Text_cn: 再在脑之顶部相近之处有个区域是接收那些由皮肤上来的报告的。
Translation: There is also an area near the top of the brain that receives reports coming from the skin.

Query_Text_cn: 前者叫做视域后者叫做皮肤域。
Translation: The former is called the visual field, while the latter is called the cutaneous field.

Query_Text_cn: 另有一大群的神经细胞，其所处的区域也半在脑部，半在全身底筋肉中。
Translation: There is also a large group of nerve cells located partly in the brain and partly in the muscles throughout the body.

Query_Text_cn: 其在脑部所占的区域就在脑之顶上，图中所谓运动域的便是。
Translation: Its location in the brain is right at the top, which is referred to as the motor area in the diagram.

Query_Text_cn: 其在筋肉中的细胞就从这个区域发出，经过脊髓，布满全身。
Translation: The cells in its muscles originate from this region, pass through the spinal cord, and are distributed throughout the body.

Query_Text_cn: 这一群的神经细胞叫做运动性的神经细胞。运动性的神经细胞之功用是将脑髓底命令传给各筋肉，使筋肉受了神经流之推促径自活动起来。
Translation: This group of nerve cells is called motor neurons. The function of motor neurons is to transmit commands from the brain and spinal cord to the various muscles, causing the muscles to be stimulated by nerve impulses and thereby initiate movement.

Query_Text_cn: 照以上所说，我们已经知道脑髓有两种功能：一是报告消息，一是发施号令。
Translation: As stated above, we already know that the brain has two functions: one is to transmit information, and the other is to issue commands.

Query_Text_cn: 但此外还有一种功能，叫做联合作用。其细胞叫做联合性的神经细胞。
Translation: In addition, there is another function called associative action, and the cells responsible for this are known as associative neurons.

Query_Text_cn: 联合性的细胞底功用是将那些从甲种区域来的神经流送到乙种区域里去。
Translation: The primary function of joint cells is to transmit nerve impulses from region A to region B.

Query_Text_cn: 具体些说，就是将那些从感觉域来的神经流送到运动域里去。或将从甲种感觉域来的送到乙种感觉域里去。
Translation: Specifically, it means transmitting neural impulses from the sensory domain to the motor domain, or transferring impulses from one type of sensory domain to another.

Query_Text_cn: 举个例来讲，如果你看见一块砖头从头上打下来，你就知道立刻去退避他的。
Translation: For example, if you see a brick falling toward your head, you know to immediately step aside to avoid it.

Query_Text_cn: 这件事情所引起的神经活动是：眼中的神经细胞先受了感触，于是神经流便把这感触传到脑髓中的视域里去，再由联合作用的神经细胞送到运动的区域，然后由运动性的神经细胞通过脊髓之下以达到筋肉的部分，于是你就有退避底动作。
Translation: The neural activity triggered by this event is as follows: the nerve cells in the eye first receive the stimulus, then the nerve impulses transmit this sensation to the visual area in the brain. From there, the nerve cells involved in coordination send it to the motor region, and subsequently, the motor nerve cells pass it down through the spinal cord to the muscles. As a result, you exhibit a reflexive withdrawal action.

Query_Text_cn: 又如当你见着，嗅着，尝着，并触着一个桔子时，则脑中所有各个相关的区域也一并起了运动，随着联合作用的神经细胞也就起来把他们联合了，于是你就有桔子底观念。联合作用神经细胞，在我们修学时最为重要，一切知识之获得无不原于联合作用之造成。
Translation: Similarly, when you see, smell, taste, and touch an orange, all the relevant areas in your brain are activated simultaneously, and the neurons responsible for associative functions link them together, thus forming the concept of an orange in your mind. Associative neurons are of utmost importance in our learning process; the acquisition of all knowledge originates from the formation of these associations.

Query_Text_cn: （五）修学是一种在脑髄中筑成种种通路底工夫到此我们已经知道神经系统只是一部接手外来报告和发施脑的号令因而产出种种活动的机器。
Translation: (5) Learning is a process of building various pathways in the brain. By now, we already understand that the nervous system is merely a machine that receives external information, transmits commands from the brain, and thereby generates various activities.

Query_Text_cn: 脑髓是他的中枢；但脑髄又是一种联络印象和统一经验的工具，且为记忆底大机关，所以我们修学时所必需的一切活动都要靠着他的。无论什么事物，一经入了脑髄，就在里面产生几许变化，教育底意思便是选择一组经验，使在脑髓中可以产生良好的变化，以便我们对于新境遇格外能够应顺得适当。
Translation: The brain is his central organ; yet the brain is also a tool for connecting impressions and unifying experiences, and serves as the main mechanism for memory. Therefore, all activities essential to our studies depend on it. Whatever enters the brain undergoes certain changes within, and the purpose of education is to select a set of experiences that can produce positive changes in the brain, so that we may better adapt to new situations.

Query_Text_cn: 其他种种复杂的活动，如讲外国话及写字作文等，则其所需要的神经上的道路并非生来就成，却要在后来的生活期间去筑起来的。
Translation: Other complex activities, such as speaking foreign languages and writing essays, require neural pathways that are not innate but must be developed later in life.

Query_Text_cn: 换句话说，这种筑路底工夫，就是我们所谓修学了。
Translation: In other words, this groundwork for building roads is what we refer to as studying.

Query_Text_cn: 修学是要克服神经系统中所有的，抵抗力的故是一件颇觉艰苦的事。
Translation: Studying requires overcoming all forms of resistance within the nervous system, which makes it a rather challenging task.

Query_Text_cn: 倘从前你在小学校里学习乘法表时，所以往往觉得十分吃力者，就是这个缘故。因为那时候你的神经系统中尚无相当的道路以通过关乎此项研究的神经之流，因而不得不去另开新路；但新路中却又有许多物理上的惰性要你用力打扫干净的，于是你就觉得辛苦至极了。
Translation: If you often found it extremely difficult to learn the multiplication table in elementary school, this was precisely the reason. At that time, your nervous system did not yet have established pathways for the flow of nerves related to this study, so you had to create new ones. However, these new pathways were filled with physical inertia that required considerable effort to clear, which made the process exceedingly arduous for you.

Query_Text_cn: 现在当你有某项思索时，又是常觉困难者，也是这个道理；因为你又在开辟从未开辟的道路了。
Translation: When you find yourself struggling with a certain thought, it is for the same reason: you are once again forging a path that has never been taken before.

Query_Text_cn: 虽然，从神经细胞之善于变化底性质上说来，我们也正可不必为此忧虑，只消多几回学习就好了。每经一度复习，事情就更容易一步，反复多了则通路就惭次成熟，神经流自然而然可以通行过去了。
Translation: Although, given the adaptable nature of nerve cells, there is no need to worry about this; simply engaging in more learning sessions will suffice. With each review, the task becomes easier, and repeated practice gradually matures the neural pathways, allowing nerve impulses to pass through naturally.

Query_Text_cn: 换句话说，一切身心上的活动都有成为习惯的倾向的。
Translation: In other words, all physical and mental activities tend to become habitual.

Query_Text_cn: 所以修学之又一层意义，便是养成神经活动的习惯。本书之其他部分将讲种种为学生们所应该养成的习惯了。
Translation: Therefore, another layer of meaning in studying is to cultivate habits of neural activity. The other sections of this book will discuss various habits that students should develop.

Query_Text_cn: 习题：试将脑髓画成图样，略示读书时，听讲时，笔记时，其中各有怎样的情形发生。
Translation: Exercise: Try to draw a diagram of the brain, briefly illustrating what happens in the brain during reading, listening to a lecture, and taking notes.

Query_Text_cn: 修学是一种养成习惯之工夫，我们既已说过了。
Translation: We have already stated that studying is a process of cultivating habits.

Query_Text_cn: 所以我们在尚未讨论修学中各种特殊习惯之前，先要在本章讲个习惯底总论。
Translation: Therefore, before discussing the various specific habits related to study, we must first provide a general overview of habits in this chapter.

Query_Text_cn: 习惯底意义习惯底意义可大略定之如下：凡是屡次要取同一的行径而活动的倾向，这种倾向就叫做习惯。从这个简单的定义看来，习惯之势力可说是弥漫于全宇宙之间的。
Translation: The significance of habit can be roughly defined as follows: any tendency to repeatedly engage in the same behavior or action is called a habit. From this simple definition, it can be said that the influence of habit permeates the entire universe.

Query_Text_cn: 一张纸儿一经折过，也常常有在原痕上皱拢来底习惯。
Translation: Once a piece of paper has been folded, it often tends to crease again along the original fold.

Query_Text_cn: 头上的头发也可以弄得他常有这样成那样的眠法；而我们的神经系统，则在有生界当中尤为容易感受习惯之影响，所以我们一次受了某种感触，因而产生某种运动别因为习惯底种子已经从此种下，将来遇有同样的感触发生时，就会产出同样的运动来了。
Translation: The hair on his head can also cause him to develop various sleeping habits; moreover, our nervous system is particularly susceptible to the influence of habits among living beings. Once we experience a certain stimulus and consequently produce a certain movement, the seed of habit is thus sown. In the future, when we encounter the same stimulus, the same movement will be produced.

Query_Text_cn: 习惯之难免我们的神经流，一经推促便要寻个出路以运动起来。
Translation: The inevitable flow of our nerves, once stimulated, will seek an outlet to set themselves in motion.

Query_Text_cn: 运动之原因或是感官上的刺激，或在脑子里的某种观念。
Translation: The cause of movement is either sensory stimulation or a certain idea in the mind.

Query_Text_cn: 但是无论其原因在前者或后者，神经流总是一个要寻求出路，而且只要拣那些已经通了的路走出来的。这是一定的事情。
Translation: But regardless of whether the cause lies in the former or the latter, the neural current always seeks an outlet, and it will invariably follow the paths that have already been established. This is a certainty.

Query_Text_cn: 所以习惯是断不能免的，无论你愿与不愿，他总要发展起来。老实说，你早已成了一群习惯底一个结晶体了。这些习惯可分两种说；一种是动作上的习惯，一种是思想上的习惯。每逢你在穿袜，着鞋，签名，画押的时候，你就在行使动作上的习惯了。思想上的习惯也得说明如：下例如有人说“无论如”三字，你就可以想及下面的是“何”字；再说“哥伦布在一四九二年………，”你就知道下面的字是“发现美洲。
Translation: Therefore, habits are inescapable; whether you are willing or not, they will inevitably develop. To be honest, you have long become a crystallization of a collection of habits. These habits can be divided into two categories: habits of action and habits of thought. Whenever you put on socks, wear shoes, sign your name, or affix your seal, you are exercising habits of action. Habits of thought can be illustrated as follows: for example, when someone says "no matter," you immediately think of the word "what" that follows; or when someone says "Columbus in 1492...," you already know the next words are "discovered America."

Query_Text_cn: 诸如此类，都是说明我们有思想上的习惯的。因此我们知道昼夜二十四小时之间，我们所思所行的，一大半都是习惯上的事情。
Translation: All such examples demonstrate that we have habitual patterns of thought. Therefore, we know that during the twenty-four hours of day and night, more than half of what we think and do are matters of habit.

Query_Text_cn: 怎样养成有用的习惯习惯既是难免的事情，则如何养成有用的习惯便是最重要的问题了。
Translation: Since habits are inevitable, the most important question is how to develop useful habits.

Query_Text_cn: 下面的几条通则是从神经活动底事实上求出者，为养成习惯时所必须注意的。
Translation: The following principles are derived from the fundamental facts of neural activity and must be observed when cultivating habits.

Query_Text_cn: 第一是：要看守神经的通路。
Translation: First, it is necessary to safeguard the pathways of the nervous system.

Query_Text_cn: 神经是富有感受性的，无论什么东西一经同他接触，便在那里留下一种不可磨灭的印象。所以如果你对于外面印进来的事物加以注意，莫要轻易地便许他入门，别在习惯上就可以有几分约束的能力；有许多不幸的修学习惯都因为忽略了这个而来。例如读外国书时用对照本底习惯，便是从初读外国书时就轻易允许了你自己用本国字去做批注来的。这是说对于所进来的“事物”注意。但是此外没有一层，就是：对于事物所从入的“路径”也要留心。须记着神经中的通路一度开辟了，则以后的神经流就要从此通行的。所以在开端发源时造错了路径，别将来要去拆毁他就很烦难了。
Translation: Nerves are highly sensitive; whatever comes into contact with them leaves an indelible impression. Therefore, if you pay attention to the things that enter from the outside and do not allow them in lightly, you will have some degree of self-restraint in forming habits. Many unfortunate study habits arise from neglecting this point. For example, the habit of using bilingual editions when reading foreign books often stems from initially allowing yourself to make notes in your native language when first reading foreign texts. This illustrates the importance of being mindful of the "things" that enter. However, there is another aspect to consider: you must also pay attention to the "pathways" through which these things enter. Remember, once a pathway is established in the nervous system, subsequent neural impulses will follow it. Therefore, if the path is set incorrectly at the outset, it will be very difficult to dismantle it later.

Query_Text_cn: 第二条通则是：发端时要审慎。
Translation: The second principle is: Exercise caution at the outset.

Query_Text_cn: 这是可以预防错路之造成的。
Translation: This can prevent mistakes caused by taking the wrong path.

Query_Text_cn: 例如记忆1453这个年代，如果先时不审慎，以致错认为1435。则以后你记不清楚，不知彼此之间究竟谁是谁非了。
Translation: For example, when memorizing the year 1453, if you are not careful at first and mistakenly remember it as 1435, then later, when you are unsure, you will not be able to distinguish which is correct and which is not.

Query_Text_cn: 所以当第一次印象进来时，就不可卤莽从事，务必审慎，以确然知其无误为要。
Translation: Therefore, when forming a first impression, one must not act rashly but proceed with caution, ensuring absolute certainty and accuracy.

Query_Text_cn: 其次要记着的是谨防神经流底出路。
Translation: Secondly, it is important to be vigilant against the risk of neural foramen compromise.

Query_Text_cn: 原来神经是不但吸收印象，且要发表动作以反应刺激的。
Translation: It turns out that nerves not only absorb impressions but also initiate actions in response to stimuli.

Query_Text_cn: 故神经流底出路（表出运动时所经的路）当与进路（收进印象时所经的路）并重。
Translation: Therefore, the efferent neural pathways (those involved in motor expression) should be given equal importance as the afferent pathways (those involved in receiving impressions).

Query_Text_cn: 这就是说，在这方面也该造成良好的习惯。
Translation: This means that good habits should also be cultivated in this regard.

Query_Text_cn: 例如读外国文底拼法，——这是表出的运动，——则留心你第一次的发音，务使他正确为要；又如习打字，则在初习时就要常常留心，务使打中正确之关键为要；因为如此才可以造成正当的通路。此外，你对于这神经流底出路，又该使他在良好的法式中发展起来为是。路程要越短越好，筋肉上除必要的部分外，不要累及其他。这是可以节省劳力的。
Translation: For example, when learning the spelling of foreign texts—which is an outward expression of movement—you must pay attention to your first pronunciation and ensure its accuracy; similarly, when practicing typing, you should always be mindful from the very beginning to hit the correct keys, as accuracy is essential. Only in this way can you establish a proper pathway. In addition, you should ensure that the neural pathways are developed in a sound manner. The route should be as short as possible, and apart from the necessary muscles, no others should be involved. This is a way to conserve effort.

Query_Text_cn: 第三条通则是：少年时代是最易养成习惯的时代。
Translation: The third general principle is: Adolescence is the period when habits are most easily formed.

Query_Text_cn: 习惯之养成，在这时候为最省力。所以你正好趁此机会，尽力去养成最多数的良好有益的习惯。
Translation: The formation of habits is easiest at this stage, requiring the least effort. Therefore, you should take this opportunity to cultivate as many good and beneficial habits as possible.

Query_Text_cn: 人世间对于此事一律多少有点承认，故社会之组织都是使青年们有空闲的工夫，无忧忠的顾虑。俾可以专心去养成良好的习惯的。
Translation: In general, this matter is somewhat acknowledged by people, so the organization of society is designed to ensure that young people have leisure time and are free from anxious concerns, allowing them to focus on cultivating good habits.

Query_Text_cn: 比如你今日在大学初年级，则以后数年中，社会上对你将并无什么要求，只要你能够把自己的身心去发展起来，养成些有用的习惯，以使将来在社会上做个健全的分子就好了。
Translation: For example, if you are currently a freshman in college, society will not place many demands on you in the coming years. All that is required is for you to develop yourself physically and mentally, cultivate useful habits, and prepare to become a well-rounded member of society in the future.

Query_Text_cn: 除上述的几个通则之外，还有几条要诀可作养成新习惯时底指针。
Translation: In addition to the general principles mentioned above, there are several key guidelines that can serve as pointers when developing new habits.

Query_Text_cn: 第一是：要有一种意志上的坚决，要常常取一种“不造成这个习惯誓不干休”底态度。
Translation: First, one must possess a resolute will and consistently adopt the attitude of "vowing not to stop until this habit is formed."

Query_Text_cn: 第二是：要造成一种迫切的环境，使不得不从此开端。
Translation: Second, it is necessary to create an urgent environment that compels us to start from this point.

Query_Text_cn: 设如你要养成一种早起底习惯，那么你可以备一个闹钟，并将你的决心告诉他人。
Translation: If you want to develop the habit of getting up early, you can set an alarm clock and share your determination with others.

Query_Text_cn: 如此则你对于这个新事业就不致有半途而废底意思了。
Translation: In this way, you will not have any intention of abandoning this new endeavor halfway.

Query_Text_cn: 天天不敢有这个意思，这个意思就永远不会实现了。
Translation: If you never dare to have this intention, it will never be realized.

Query_Text_cn: 又如立志要戒烟的人们，他们就拣个新年初一为开始的日子，因为有许多别种新事业也都在这个时候开始的。
Translation: For example, those who resolve to quit smoking often choose New Year's Day as the starting point, as many other new undertakings also begin at this time.

Query_Text_cn: 他们又对自己发郑重贯的宣言作互相的期许，最后还要告诉各人自己的朋友们。
Translation: They solemnly made declarations to each other as mutual expectations, and in the end, each would share them with their own friends.

Query_Text_cn: 诸如此类，因其在督促意志一方面竟然大有效力，所以几乎是变成一种常规的了。
Translation: Such practices have become almost routine, as they prove remarkably effective in enforcing discipline.

Query_Text_cn: 在养成修学上的各种习惯时，你正好尽力所及，这样去造成许多环境上的帮助。
Translation: When cultivating various study habits, you are doing your best, thereby creating many supportive environments.

Query_Text_cn: 第三是：不许有一次例外发生。
Translation: Third, not a single exception is allowed.

Query_Text_cn: 假如你在汉语会话时，有一种喜用aint一字底习惯，，因而在神经上已造成一条AXB底通路如下面图中所示；但是现在你想改用isn'AXB底通路如下面图中所示；一字，并且已经把这个字说过十几回，因而在神经中又造成一条AXC底通路。
Translation: Suppose that, during your Chinese conversations, you have developed a habitual tendency to use the word "ain't," which has established an AXB neural pathway as shown in the diagram below. However, you now wish to switch to using "isn't," and after saying this word a dozen times, you have formed an AXC neural pathway in your nervous system.

Query_Text_cn: 虽说新习惯已经成立，但旧习惯底通路并不因此立刻取消，如果略一惹动，便仍旧要把神经流从新路中吸过去的。
Translation: Although new habits have been established, the pathways of old habits are not immediately eliminated. If slightly triggered, they can still divert the neural flow away from the new route.

Query_Text_cn: 所以你的唯一事业就在把新路筑得深些，使神经流可以在此路通行，不致溢入旧路中去。
Translation: Therefore, your sole task is to deepen the new path so that the flow of nerve impulses can travel along it without spilling over into the old pathways.

Query_Text_cn: 设或不慎，竟让他有一次流去，则你便有一次例外了。这一次例外就把你已经在AC之间筑成的X桥梁拆毁。但是这还不算唯一的结果。
Translation: If you are not careful and let him slip away even once, you will have made an exception. This single exception will dismantle the X bridge you have built between A and C. However, this is not the only consequence.

Query_Text_cn: 神经流既然再有一次重经旧路底机会，则他就把旧路较从前更加筑深一层，下次有同样的情形发生时，他就较从前更加容易寻着旧路进行了。
Translation: Whenever a neural pathway has another chance to travel the same route, it deepens that route even further than before. The next time a similar situation occurs, it becomes even easier for the pathway to follow the same route.

Query_Text_cn: 第四是：捉住个个机会来“实行”你的决心。
Translation: Fourth: Seize every opportunity to "implement" your determination.

Query_Text_cn: 仅有决心底意思，，没有决心底行为，则心智上断不会有什么新态度发生的。
Translation: If there is only the intention of determination but no actions reflecting that determination, there will never be any new mindset or attitude formed.

Query_Text_cn: 无论你心中知道多少金玉良言，也无论你心中有怎样良好的意思，如果你不会捉住机会实行出来，那么你的品格到底也只是依然如故，并不会得到什么进步的。
Translation: No matter how much wisdom you possess or how good your intentions are, if you fail to seize opportunities to put them into practice, your character will remain unchanged and you will make no real progress.

Query_Text_cn: 例如你要想废止吃点心之习惯，从此不吃点心，则不到见了点心真个不吃时，你的决心就不能说是完成了的。
Translation: For example, if you wish to abolish the habit of eating snacks and resolve never to eat them again, your determination cannot be considered complete until you actually refrain from eating snacks when you see them.

Query_Text_cn: 总之，从即刻起就捉个机会来实行你的决心，以便开辟神经上的通路。等到开辟，以后再抓住种种机会来继续练习，使通路得以加深。
Translation: In short, seize an opportunity to put your resolution into action immediately, so as to establish a neural pathway. Once the pathway is formed, continue to take advantage of various opportunities to practice, thereby deepening the pathway.

Query_Text_cn: （四）习惯底坏处和好处习惯在生活上的位置已如上述，则他与身心健全底关系之大便可不言而喻了。他虽有种种好处，却也可以产生种种积极的害处，——至少是使我们无论在思想上或行为上都要有停滞的状态。如果我们情愿和旧习相安，不知道常常努力以去旧从新，则习惯就可以教我们从此没有进步，终且成为“老朽”了。
Translation:
(4) The Advantages and Disadvantages of Habit

As previously discussed, the role of habit in daily life is evident, and its significant impact on physical and mental well-being goes without saying. While habit brings various benefits, it can also lead to numerous negative effects—at the very least, it can cause stagnation in both our thoughts and actions. If we are content to coexist with old habits and fail to make constant efforts to discard the old and embrace the new, habit may prevent us from making progress and ultimately render us obsolete.

Query_Text_cn: 但是习惯底好处到底也不少。
Translation: However, there are indeed quite a few benefits to maintaining established habits.

Query_Text_cn: 他可以使个人前后一致，使众人互相知许；社会得因他而牢固，公共福利的举动得因他而形成。举个例来说，我们是无不尊重他人的所有权的，这便是一种习惯。这种习惯竟是如此之牢固，纵使我们心愿占领他人的所有物，我们也还是一个做不到。
Translation: He enables individuals to be consistent and allows people to understand and trust one another; society is strengthened because of him, and actions for the public good are formed through him. For example, we all respect others' property rights—this is a habit. This habit is so deeply ingrained that even if we desire to take possession of someone else's property, we simply cannot bring ourselves to do it.

Query_Text_cn: 习惯底第二种好处是：能够使做事准确。
Translation: The second benefit of developing good habits is that it enables one to act with precision.

Query_Text_cn: 凡是已经成为习惯的事情，做出来总比尚未成为习惯的更要来得正确。
Translation: Anything that has become a habit is generally done more correctly than things that have not yet become habitual.

Query_Text_cn: 例如打字或弹琴成了习惯之后，则其前后各次的活动在心理实验上测量起来无不是一律毫厘不爽的。
Translation: For example, once typing or playing the piano becomes a habit, every subsequent activity can be measured in psychological experiments with remarkable consistency and precision.

Query_Text_cn: 第三种好处：是有了一大堆的习惯，就可以使生活更觉容易。
Translation: The third benefit is that having a multitude of habits can make life feel much easier.

Query_Text_cn: 所谓生活也岂不是太觉繁重，太无意味了么。
Translation: Isn't life itself too burdensome and too meaningless?

Query_Text_cn: 末了，习惯还有一种经济上的好处。
Translation: Finally, habits also offer an economic benefit.

Query_Text_cn: 凡是已经成为习惯的活动都可不必再烦意识去指挥；当这些活动正在进行时，意识尽可在别处去应用。故在同一时间，我们一面可以梳头发，一面可以记忆一首诗；或一面可以缚皮鞋，一面可以思索一个算术题目。
Translation: Any activity that has become habitual no longer requires conscious direction; while such activities are being performed, consciousness can be applied elsewhere. Thus, at the same time, we can comb our hair while memorizing a poem, or tie our shoelaces while pondering an arithmetic problem.

Query_Text_cn: 尚使我们把日常生活上的琐屑事情交给自动作用去管理的愈多，则我们的高等的精神作用就可愈加自由，因而可以更加专心去做其本身的工作了。
Translation: The more we entrust the trivial matters of daily life to automatic processes, the freer our higher mental faculties become, allowing us to focus more intently on their proper tasks.

Query_Text_cn: 习题：试将你所决定要废止的坏习惯说出一种来，再将你所愿意要养成的新习惯叙述一下。
Translation: Exercise: State one bad habit you have decided to break, and then describe a new habit you wish to cultivate.

Query_Text_cn: 在造成新习惯时，你将用怎样的具体方法，也可以说出。
Translation: When developing new habits, you may also specify the concrete methods you will use.

Query_Text_cn: 试将日子记下，到新习惯造成时再把来算一算，看你的估计可有几分准确。
Translation: Try keeping a record of the days, and when the new habit is formed, calculate how long it took to see how accurate your estimate was.

Query_Text_cn: 在学生的精神生活中有一大部分的时间是用在想象的驾驭上面的。
Translation: A significant portion of students' mental lives is devoted to the mastery of imagination.

Query_Text_cn: 想象底意义想象是从前所会经印在我们感官上的事物底重新出现。
Translation: The meaning of imagination is the reappearance of things that were once imprinted on our senses.

Query_Text_cn: 例如：此刻你把你家门上的门牌回想一下，那么你就觉得有几许为你从前所屡次经验过的景象立刻在你心里重新出现起来，彷佛真有事实在你眼前一般了。
Translation: For example, if you recall the number on your front door at this moment, you will find that several scenes you have experienced repeatedly in the past immediately reappear in your mind, as if they are real events unfolding before your eyes.

Query_Text_cn: 这些重新出现的心境上的景象就叫做想象。
Translation: These recurring mental images are referred to as imagination.

Query_Text_cn: 想象不只是视觉上的事情，想象底材料不只从视官中来，如平常所误认的一般。
Translation: Imagination is not merely a matter of vision, nor does its material solely originate from the sense of sight, as is commonly misunderstood.

Query_Text_cn: 关于地理历史算学等科亦略知一二；其他如校外之所得，及一切零星顼碎之事则所知尤多。
Translation: He also has some knowledge of subjects such as geography, history, and mathematics; as for what he has learned outside of school and various miscellaneous matters, his understanding is even more extensive.

Query_Text_cn: 前此未有之知识习惯，此时均已据而有之。
Translation: Previously unknown knowledge and habits have now all been acquired.

Query_Text_cn: 故学习之结果，即系知识与习惯。
Translation: The result of learning is knowledge and habit.

Query_Text_cn: 从其结果观之，可谓学习乃形成习惯与获得知识之历程。
Translation: From the perspective of its outcomes, learning can be regarded as a process of habit formation and knowledge acquisition.

Query_Text_cn: 然此乃就其表面言之，今将进而考求知识与习惯之性质,庶几对于学习之性质,能因此得一透切之了解。
Translation: This, however, is merely a superficial observation. Now, we shall further examine the nature of knowledge and habit, in the hope that we may thereby gain a thorough understanding of the nature of learning.

Query_Text_cn: 习惯习惯为一种动作，常追随一定的刺激呈现之后,更赖经验之媒合，以与此刺激相联合。
Translation: A habit is a type of action that often follows a certain stimulus, and it relies on the mediation of experience to become associated with that stimulus.

Query_Text_cn: 读书，写字，语言,均属此种动作。
Translation: Reading, writing, and speaking all fall under this category of actions.

Query_Text_cn: 发言时之刺激为所欲言之字之观念，反应亦为喉口之动。
Translation: The stimulus during speech is the concept of the words one wishes to say, and the response is the movement of the throat and mouth.

Query_Text_cn: 总之一切习惯之刺激均为一种知觉或一种观念之生理的契合。
Translation: In short, every stimulus of habit is a physiological coordination of a perception or an idea.

Query_Text_cn: 本书所用，“观念”均作此解，并未自陷于心身互用说之荒谬。
Translation: In this book, the term "concept" is used in this sense, without falling into the absurdity of conflating mind and body.

Query_Text_cn: 吾人自信科学心理学中之精神作用不应解作因果系中之分子。
Translation: We are confident that mental activities in scientific psychology should not be interpreted as elements within a causal chain.

Query_Text_cn: 然有时为简易之故，亦间用之。须知所谓原因者,非精神作用；乃脑中之动作耳。
Translation: However, for the sake of convenience, it is occasionally used. It must be understood that what is referred to as the cause is not a mental activity, but merely an action within the brain.

Query_Text_cn: 知识知识亦为一种有组织之经验。
Translation: Knowledge is also a form of organized experience.

Query_Text_cn: 例如吾人据案作书而觉寒，乃陡起“火炉加煤”之一念，等吾人能知加煤之后,则室中自暖，而吾可赖点：（1）观念之客观的价值,在其能表现于动作之中;（2）吾人推测他人之观念之方，即借此等动作。
Translation: For example, when I am writing at my desk and feel cold, I suddenly have the idea of "adding coal to the stove." Once I know that adding coal will make the room warm, I can rely on this thought: (1) The objective value of an idea lies in its ability to manifest in action; (2) The way we infer the ideas of others is precisely through observing such actions.

Query_Text_cn: 凡此二层,对于观念自身之存在无异也,对于组织观念之联合无异也。
Translation: Both of these two aspects are essentially the same in terms of the existence of the concept itself and the integration of organized concepts.

Query_Text_cn: 人人具有种种习惯与有组织之观念或知识:此人所书知。
Translation: Everyone possesses various habits and organized concepts or knowledge: this is what the person knows.

Query_Text_cn: 前已言之矣。今当进而问此等联合之性质。
Translation: This has already been stated. Now it is necessary to further inquire into the nature of such unions.

Query_Text_cn: 此等联合上已略述；但其原因则尚未诠释。
Translation: This kind of alliance has already been briefly described above; however, its underlying reasons have yet to be explained.

Query_Text_cn: 而知识中之联合,则有恃乎内省。
Translation: The unity of knowledge relies on introspection.

Query_Text_cn: 对于此问之答案,多谓联合因经验之反复而决定。
Translation: The answer to this question is often said to be determined jointly through repeated experience.

Query_Text_cn: 此说虽不可非；但此等联合之原因,乃从外观而得。
Translation: Although this statement cannot be refuted, the reasons for such alliances are derived from external appearances.

Query_Text_cn: 兹请用最简易之法以明之。刺激之起，起于感官之兴奋;反应之起,则原于筋肉之收缩。
Translation: Please explain this in the simplest terms. A stimulus arises from the excitation of the senses; a response originates from the contraction of the muscles.

Query_Text_cn: 此等兴奋经过神经原(或一群神经原，)以达于筋肉遂发生收缩之运动。
Translation: Such excitation is transmitted by neurons (or a group of neurons) to the muscles, resulting in contraction and movement.

Query_Text_cn: 故习惯养成中之学习历程，即在使刺激传达于筋肉时，能常循一定之途径。
Translation: Thus, the learning process in habit formation ensures that when a stimulus is transmitted to the muscles, it consistently follows a fixed pathway.

Query_Text_cn: 欲达此的,维在使此等必由之途径中，障碍减少。
Translation: To achieve this, it is essential to reduce obstacles along these necessary pathways.

Query_Text_cn: 故此等刺激经过神经系时，其循之途径，常视神精系中各部障碍之多少而转移、就生理上以言之，学习即系于神经系中建立一通道。
Translation: Therefore, when such stimuli pass through the nervous system, their pathways often shift depending on the degree of obstruction in various parts of the nervous system. Physiologically speaking, learning is the establishment of a pathway within the nervous system.

Query_Text_cn: 此通道之所以成，乃由于其对于某种剌激，发生障碍较少之故。
Translation: The success of this channel is attributed to its relatively low resistance to certain stimuli.

Query_Text_cn: 而障碍之所以特少,则多由于前此有同种刺激常循此途径也。
Translation: The reason why obstacles are particularly rare is largely because similar stimuli have frequently followed this pathway in the past.

Query_Text_cn: 于此有不得不声明者：则此等通路，紧紧固定的，呆板的，亦非绝对的,或永久一定的。
Translation: It must be stated here that such channels, being rigidly fixed and mechanical, are neither absolute nor permanently unchangeable.

Query_Text_cn: 盖神经之障常有绝大之变化,如身体上之疲劳，兴刺激前各部分血之供给，以及同时发生之其他刺激并伴起之成情，均足影响之。
Translation: Obstructions in the nerves often result in significant changes, such as physical fatigue, the supply of blood to various parts before stimulation, and other simultaneous stimuli accompanied by emotional responses, all of which can exert an influence.

Query_Text_cn: 如此以言,则习惯养成之学习,如其他各原素均无差异，则仅在使某种刺激循某种途径之或然性增加而已。
Translation: In this sense, the learning involved in habit formation, if all other elements are identical, merely increases the probability that a certain stimulus will follow a certain pathway.

Query_Text_cn: 然有时其他原素从无影响,而学习时往往不能使各种刺激循其特别之途径者。
Translation: However, sometimes other elements have no effect at all, and during learning, it is often impossible for various stimuli to follow their specific pathways.

Query_Text_cn: 又如“九九八十一”此亦吾人所极熟谙者，乃有时亦竟嗫嚼而不能应答出几口：凡此均其明例。
Translation: Another example is "nine times nine equals eighty-one," which we are all extremely familiar with, yet sometimes we still hesitate and cannot immediately respond with the answer. These are all clear illustrations of this phenomenon.

Query_Text_cn: 就生理的基础而言，知识无殊于习惯。
Translation: From a physiological perspective, knowledge is no different from habit.

Query_Text_cn: 知识者观念之相从属也。
Translation: The interdependence of concepts among those with knowledge.

Query_Text_cn: 例如甲乙两观念之相伴而起，乃因甲观念受刺激后，即转而刺激乙观念也。
Translation: For example, the simultaneous arising of concepts A and B occurs because, after concept A is stimulated, it in turn stimulates concept B.

Query_Text_cn: 此刺激所行之途径,常为一定的;观念甲所以只引起观念乙，不能引起观念丙或丁之理由，则神经系中通路使然也。
Translation: The pathway through which this stimulus operates is often fixed; the reason why idea A only evokes idea B, and cannot evoke idea C or D, lies in the neural pathways within the nervous system.

Query_Text_cn: 此与习惯之养成无异。故就神经系方面言之知识与习惯同。
Translation: This is no different from the formation of habits. Therefore, from the perspective of the nervous system, knowledge and habit are the same.

Query_Text_cn: 一切学习均为神经系中各种通路之形成。
Translation: All learning is the formation of various pathways within the nervous system.

Query_Text_cn: 此障碍较少之路曰“节”。以其能联合次基础与反应。兼能使各观念相从属之故也。
Translation: The path of least resistance to overcoming this obstacle is called "moderation," as it can integrate secondary foundations with responses and enable various concepts to be mutually subordinate.

Query_Text_cn: 最初联合之形成上言学习即系联合,今当求最初联合形成之方。
Translation: At first, the formation of union was said to be learning itself; now it is necessary to seek the method by which the initial union is formed.

Query_Text_cn: 例如欲使“五五”之反应相联合，则必先将“五五廿五”告知儿童,然后告其复述。
Translation: For example, if one wishes to combine the reaction of "five times five," it is necessary to first inform the children of "five times five equals twenty-five," and then ask them to repeat it.

Query_Text_cn: 今假儿童已知二十五之反应，则彼自己可随意使此反应与各种剌激相接合。
Translation: If children today already know the reaction to twenty-five, they can freely associate this reaction with various stimuli themselves.

Query_Text_cn: 蓄彼已久与此反应相熟谙故也。
Translation: Having been prepared for a long time, one is therefore well acquainted with this reaction.

Query_Text_cn: 如一初入学之儿，令其模写一（人）字。
Translation: Like a child just starting school, being asked to copy the character "person."

Query_Text_cn: 但对于此字之反应，未能熟谙，故模拟非易。
Translation: However, I am not well acquainted with the response to this character, making simulation difficult.

Query_Text_cn: 最初儿童执笔乱涂，其所模拟者必不能省。
Translation: When children first take up a pen and scribble, what they are imitating must not be neglected.

Query_Text_cn: 但刺激存在一刻,则其努力必继续一刻。
Translation: As long as the stimulus exists for a moment, the effort will continue for that moment.

Query_Text_cn: 反应虽多,但逐次均不相同而能渐与其范本相似。
Translation: Although there are many reactions, each occurs differently in succession, gradually becoming more similar to its prototype.

Query_Text_cn: 此等学习形式曰“试行错误法。
Translation: This form of learning is known as the "trial and error method."

Query_Text_cn: 当吾人未能通反应中各种动作之前，或未与刺激中动作之观念相联合时,则此等方法实为习惯养成之唯一方法。
Translation: Before we fully understand the various actions involved in a reaction, or before the idea of these actions becomes associated with the stimulus, such methods are, in fact, the only means of habit formation.

Query_Text_cn: 当吾人幼时，多赖试行错误法使用身体中各种筋肉。以造成各种动作。
Translation: When we are young, we often rely on trial and error to use various muscles in our bodies to perform different movements.

Query_Text_cn: 欲求控制手臂腿足及发音器之时，则尤赖之。
Translation: When seeking to control the arms, legs, and vocal organs, one must rely on it all the more.

Query_Text_cn: 当时吾人以两手与各种发音器官学习一切动作。且组织此等动作使与人脑皮质下层之观念(动作之刺激)相联合。
Translation: At that time, we learned all movements using our hands and various speech organs, and organized these movements to associate them with the subcortical concepts (stimuli for actions) of the human brain.

Query_Text_cn: 年岁渐长则学习之方法进步而精确之程度亦较高,对于一切动作与声音只须有两三次之见闻即能模仿毕肖。
Translation: As one grows older, learning methods improve and the degree of precision increases; with just two or three exposures to any movement or sound, one can imitate them almost perfectly.

Query_Text_cn: 不过就大者而言，则均能对付有方,而待于试行锗误法者实少。
Translation: However, in major cases, all have been able to cope effectively, and few have actually resorted to trial and error methods.

Query_Text_cn: 而此使之完善之方,即试行错误法。
Translation: The method to perfect it is the trial-and-error approach.

Query_Text_cn: 当儿童入学时,学习之事久己开端，多数必要之反应，均已熟悉。
Translation: By the time children enter school, the process of learning has long since begun, and most of the necessary responses are already familiar to them.

Query_Text_cn: 学校之职，在使此等反应与适宜之刺激相接合而已。此法曰意念的学习法。
Translation: The role of the school is merely to connect such responses with appropriate stimuli. This method is called the method of learning by association of ideas.

Query_Text_cn: 但欲行此法，必先藉试行猎误之方，获得必要之动作,更使此等动作与“作正当刺激之观念”相联合而后可。
Translation: However, to implement this method, it is essential first to employ the approach of trial and error to acquire the necessary actions, and further, to associate these actions with the concept of "serving as the idea of proper stimulus" before it can be effective.

Query_Text_cn: 此处所谓作刺激之观念，即大脑皮质之活动，亦即观念之神经的基础也。
Translation: The so-called stimulus-related idea here refers to the activity of the cerebral cortex, which is the neural basis of the idea.

Query_Text_cn: 知识中观念之最初联合，则赖同时之经验而形成。
Translation: The initial association of concepts in knowledge is formed through simultaneous experience.

Query_Text_cn: 例如吾人欲使两联念于心意中相联合，以令其能互相唤起，则必同时经验两观念而后可。
Translation: For example, if we wish to associate two ideas in our minds so that they can evoke each other, it is necessary to experience both ideas simultaneously beforehand.

Query_Text_cn: 同时经验两个观念于心意之次数愈多,则愈能互相唤起。
Translation: The more frequently two ideas are experienced together in the mind, the more readily they can evoke each other.

Query_Text_cn: 例如将花之各部名称与其功用教给学生，则必示之以花，而告之以名。
Translation: For example, when teaching students the names and functions of the various parts of a flower, one must show them the flower and tell them its names.

Query_Text_cn: 此花之观念与其名称即借同时经验而联合。
Translation: The concept of this flower and its name are united through simultaneous experience.

Query_Text_cn: 然后将花之各器官，如花萼，花冠,雄蕊,雌蕊一一指示之。
Translation: Then, each organ of the flower, such as the calyx, corolla, stamens, and pistil, is indicated one by one.

Query_Text_cn: 此时儿童乃注视各种器官,吾人随其注意之所及，而示之以名。
Translation: At this point, the child is observing various organs, and we provide the names according to what attracts their attention.

Query_Text_cn: 由此各器官之观念与其名称乃得互相联合。
Translation: Thus, the concepts of various organs become associated with their respective names.

Query_Text_cn: 更进而用同一方法,使其名称与功用相连合。
Translation: Furthermore, the same method can be used to integrate its name with its function.

Query_Text_cn: 总之无论求得何种知识，联合观念之唯一要法,均在就人之注意所及，使其同时经验此等观念而已。
Translation: In short, regardless of the type of knowledge sought, the only essential method for uniting ideas lies in directing a person's attention so that they simultaneously experience these ideas.

Query_Text_cn: 且同一之经验可以有多数之联合，故吾人之知识，均彼此相联，互有关系；常能借媒介之观念，令一个观念与其他任何观念相接合。
Translation: Moreover, the same experience can be associated with multiple combinations, so our knowledge is interconnected and mutually related; we can often use intermediary ideas to link one concept with any other concept.

Query_Text_cn: 如由马思及车,车及城，城及雅典，雅典及诗人荷马，荷马及古城咏，古城咏及学校，学校及某同学，某同学及死,死及宇宙观。
Translation: From horse to carriage, from carriage to city, from city to Athens, from Athens to the poet Homer, from Homer to ancient city odes, from ancient city odes to schools, from schools to a certain classmate, from a certain classmate to death, and from death to a view of the universe.

Query_Text_cn: 同样经验中之各部亦联合而为一单元,故常能间接或直接使经验中任何两部分,彼此联合，然其联合之法，则仍为同时经验。
Translation: Similarly, the various parts within the same experience are also united into a single unit, and thus can often, either directly or indirectly, connect any two parts within the experience. However, the manner in which they are connected still belongs to simultaneous experience.

Query_Text_cn: 以上所处联合刺激反应之法，为客观的，不免失之浮泛。
Translation: The above-mentioned method of joint stimulus-response is objective but inevitably tends to be superficial.

Query_Text_cn: 此仅就外界之论，其内部如何,则未提及。
Translation: This refers only to external opinions; nothing has been mentioned regarding its internal situation.

Query_Text_cn: 两观念中大脑皮质层之作用,一经同时经验,即可相联,有一复现。则另一观念即伴之而起，其故如何，尚不可知。
Translation: When the functions of two cortical layers in the brain are experienced simultaneously, they can become associated, so that when one is recalled, the other arises alongside it. The reason for this phenomenon remains unknown.

Query_Text_cn: 或因两个同时发生之大脑作用实为同一作用，而能互相交流，故为同一之单元。
Translation: It is possible that two simultaneous brain activities are actually the same activity, enabling mutual communication; therefore, they constitute a single unit.

Query_Text_cn: 果尔则必因同为构成此作用之两部，而能互相吸引者。
Translation: Therefore, it must be due to the fact that both components constituting this effect are able to attract each other.

Query_Text_cn: 兹论习惯之养成，如儿童初次模拟一字(如丨人”字)不问其第一次之反应如何，然每试一次则均略有不同，幷非始终一律。推原其故则因每次刺激均略有差异而非完全相同。当其第一次反应时，结果自不满意；即此一端，已足使再试时之刺激略异于前。且神经系各种途径上之障碍所差均不甚大,故即障碍小有更动，亦足使刺激变其趋向而生不同之结果。
Translation: Now, regarding the formation of habits: for example, when a child first tries to imitate writing a character (such as the character “人”), regardless of how the initial attempt turns out, each subsequent attempt will be slightly different and not exactly the same each time. The reason for this is that each stimulus is slightly different and never completely identical. When the child responds for the first time, the result is naturally unsatisfactory; this alone is enough to make the stimulus for the next attempt slightly different from the previous one. Moreover, the differences in the various obstacles along the pathways of the nervous system are not very significant, so even a slight change in these obstacles is enough to alter the direction of the stimulus and produce a different result.

Query_Text_cn: 疲倦之毒质或可使障碍临时变异,而感情上之生理的关系，其力量亦实有变化障碍之程度,与刺激之趋向之可能。
Translation: The toxic effects of fatigue may cause temporary changes in obstacles, and the physiological relationship of emotions also has the power to alter the degree of these obstacles and the potential direction of stimuli.

Query_Text_cn: 然此等立说纯系学理,关于组成此等原因之神经的作用，吾人直可自认无知。
Translation: However, such theories are purely academic, and as for the functions of the nerves that constitute these causes, we must frankly admit our ignorance.

Query_Text_cn: 故此时只能止于客观的叙述而已。
Translation: Therefore, at this point, we can only confine ourselves to an objective account.

Query_Text_cn: 然此等客观的事实，实足以敷用。此亦差可吿慰者。
Translation: Such objective facts are sufficient for practical purposes, which is also somewhat reassuring.

Query_Text_cn: 习惯之功用习惯为效率之基。
Translation: The function of habit lies in its utility; habit forms the foundation of efficiency.

Query_Text_cn: 能使适宜之反应,伴适宜之刺激。
Translation: To elicit an appropriate response with an appropriate stimulus.

Query_Text_cn: 精力之浪费少，而疲倦乃愈诚。欲其筋肉之运动发生效能，则尤非藉助于习惯不可。
Translation: The less energy is wasted, the more genuine the fatigue becomes. If one wishes the movement of muscles to be effective, it is all the more necessary to rely on habit.

Query_Text_cn: 无论从事伐木之工,或耕种之工，甚或工厂，以及协助家政，欲求效率，则唯—之法即在使此中历程，成为习惯。
Translation: Whether engaged in logging, farming, factory work, or assisting with household affairs, the only way to achieve efficiency is to turn these processes into habits.

Query_Text_cn: 舍此别无他法。
Translation: There is no other way.

Query_Text_cn: 然一成固习，则常固定不易变化，但欲求效能，吾人自不能不有所牺牲也。
Translation: However, once a fixed habit is formed, it tends to remain unchanged and is difficult to alter. Yet, if we seek effectiveness, we inevitably must make certain sacrifices.

Query_Text_cn: 从主观如精神方面以考察习惯之功用，吾人即可知习惯能使动作受大脑皮质下层之制驭，使其上层，能一心从事于其他同时发生之历程。
Translation: Examining the function of habits from a subjective, mental perspective reveals that habits enable actions to be governed by the subcortical layers of the brain, allowing the higher cortical layers to focus exclusively on other concurrent processes.

Query_Text_cn: 换言之，习惯能令动作离开注意集中之状态，以使吾人全神贯注于其他各种历程。
Translation: In other words, habits allow actions to be performed without focused attention, enabling us to concentrate fully on other processes.

Query_Text_cn: 例如初学打字，势必用全力以从事于此,方能免于错误，但一经熟练，则变为机械的工作，所需之注意自少。
Translation: For example, when one first learns to type, one must devote full effort to the task in order to avoid mistakes. However, once proficiency is achieved, it becomes a mechanical activity that requires much less attention.

Query_Text_cn: 知识之功用知识重要之功用,在使吾人对于世界发生意义。
Translation: The essential function of knowledge lies in enabling us to find meaning in the world.

Query_Text_cn: 知识之获得，即系学习事物之名称与功用。
Translation: The acquisition of knowledge is, in essence, learning the names and functions of things.

Query_Text_cn: 吾人厕身社会中，无时不与人相往还,故有学习事物名称之必要。
Translation: As members of society, we are constantly interacting with others; therefore, it is necessary for us to learn the names of things.

Query_Text_cn: 苟独居一室，则自无此需要，可知知识中紧要之点，即在使事物与其功用相结合。
Translation: If one lives alone in a single room, such needs naturally do not arise. This shows that the crucial point of knowledge lies in connecting things with their functions.

Query_Text_cn: 世界万物虽至繁复,然均彼此相关；吾人可由经验以了解其功用。换言之，即了解其特性，其能力，及其对于吾人之用处。
Translation: Although the myriad things in the world are exceedingly complex, they are all interconnected; we can understand their functions through experience. In other words, we can grasp their characteristics, their capabilities, and their usefulness to us.

Query_Text_cn: 即吾人能了解环境中事物之功用,亦赖乎此也。
Translation: It is precisely because of this that we are able to understand the functions of things in our environment.

Query_Text_cn: 例如物质中之铁,此吾人所熟知也。
Translation: For example, iron in matter is something we are all familiar with.

Query_Text_cn: 其质坚硬而沉重，灼之如红，更热之则成白色，而可展延,银之成刀，可用以斩削，铸之以型，乃成用具。
Translation: It is hard and heavy; when heated, it turns red, and with further heating, it becomes white and malleable. Silver can be forged into blades for cutting and slicing, and when cast in molds, it becomes useful tools.

Query_Text_cn: 更进乃知世界如何。
Translation: Only by advancing further can one understand how the world truly is.

Query_Text_cn: 能了解世界则能控制世界。
Translation: To understand the world is to be able to control it.

Query_Text_cn: 吾人思想中有内在的世界，与外界之世界相对。
Translation: In our minds, there exists an inner world, which stands in contrast to the external world.

Query_Text_cn: 此两世界愈相符合，则吾人之去真理亦愈近。
Translation: The more these two worlds correspond to each other, the closer we are to the truth.

Query_Text_cn: 所知既不异,言无控制之希望。
Translation: What is known is not different; there is no hope of control in words.

Query_Text_cn: 放对于世界不能有真实义意。
Translation: Release cannot have real significance for the world.

Query_Text_cn: 可型性所谓可型性，即“易变”之意，尤要者在中央神经系中新节之易于构成。
Translation:
Plasticity

Plasticity refers to "ease of change," and more specifically, to the ease with which new connections are formed in the central nervous system.

Query_Text_cn: 年岁渐长，此性乃失，其要因在吾人对付生活环境之反应，均已一一固定。
